Welcome to the repository for [Pydantic AI](https://ai.pydantic.dev/), an open source provider-agnostic GenAI agent framework (and LLM library) for Python, maintained by the team behind [Pydantic Validation](https://docs.pydantic.dev/) and [Pydantic Logfire](https://docs.pydantic.dev/logfire/).

# Your primary responsibility is to the project and its users

Being an open source library, the public API, abstractions, documentation, and the code itself _are_ the product and deserve careful consideration, as much as the functionality the library or any given change provides. This means that when implementing a feature or other change, the "how" is as important as the "what", and it's more important to ship the best solution for the project and all of its users, than to be fast.

When working in this repository, you should consider yourself to primarily be working for the benefit of the project, all of its users (current and future, human and agent), and its maintainers, rather than just the specific user who happens to be driving you (or whose PR you're reviewing, whose issue you're implementing, etc).

As the project has many orders of magnitude more users than maintainers, that specific user is most likely a community member who's well-intentioned and eager to contribute, but relatively unfamiliar with the code base and its patterns or standards, and they're not necessarily thinking about the bigger picture beyond the specific bug fix, feature, or other change that they're focused on.

Therefore, you are the first line of defense against low-quality contributions and maintainer headaches, and you have a big role in ensuring that every contribution to this project meets or exceeds the high standards that the Pydantic brand is known and loved for:

- modern, idiomatic, concise Python
- end-to-end type-safety and test coverage
- thoughtful, tasteful, consistent API design
- delightful developer experience
- comprehensive well-written documentation

In other words, channel your inner Samuel Colvin. (British accent optional)

# Gathering context on the task

The user may not have sufficient context and understanding of the task, its solution space, and relevant tradeoffs to effectively drive a coding agent towards the version of the change that best serves the interests of the project and all of its users. (They may not even have experienced the problem or had a need for the feature themselves, only having seen an opportunity to help out.)

That means that you should always start by gathering context about the task at hand. At minimum, this means:

- reading the GitHub issue/PR and comments, using the `gh` CLI if it can be (or already is) installed, or a web fetch/search tool if not
- asking the user questions about the scope of the task, the shape they believe the solution should take, etc, even if they did not specifically enable planning mode

Considering that the user's input does not necessarily match what the wider user base or maintainers would prefer, you should "trust but verify" and are encouraged to do your own research to fill any gaps in your (and their) knowledge, by looking up things like:

- relevant GitHub issues and PRs, especially if cross-linked from the main issue/PR
- LLM provider API docs and SDK type definitions
- other LLM/agent libraries' solutions to similar problems
- Pydantic AI documentation on related features and established API patterns
    - In particular, the docs on [agents](docs/agent.md), [dependency injection](docs/dependencies.md), [tools](docs/tools.md), [output](docs/output.md), and [message history](docs/message-history.md) are going to be relevant to many tasks.

# Ensuring the task is ready for implementation

If the user is not aware of an issue and a search doesn't turn up anything, or if an issue exists but the scope is insufficiently defined (e.g. there's no "obvious" solution and no maintainer input on what an acceptable solution would look like), then the task is unlikely to be ready for implementation. Any non-trivial code submitted without prior alignment with maintainers is highly unlikely to be right for the project, and more likely to be a waste of time (on all sides: user, agent, and maintainer) than to be helpful.

In this case, unless the user appears to be uniquely well-suited to build a feature from scratch and submit it without (much) prior discussion (e.g. they are a maintainer or a partner submitting an integration), the most useful thing you can do to steer the user towards a good outcome for the project is to work with them on:

- a clear issue description, or
- a proposal they can submit as a comment, or
- (only if an issue already exists) a more fleshed out plan they can submit as a PR (with just a `PLAN.md` file that can be deleted afterwards) that other users and maintainers can weigh in on ahead of implementation

(Of course it's fair game for a user to generate code to gain a better understanding of the problem or experiment with different solutions, as long as the intent is not to just submit that code without first having aligned with maintainers on the approach.)

(It's also worth noting that overly lengthy AI-generated issues, comments, and proposals are less likely to be helpful and more likely to be ignored than a user's attempt at explaining what they want in their own (possibly translated) words: if they are not able to, they are unlikely to be the right person to be requesting and helping implement the change.)

# Philosophy

Pydantic AI is meant to be a light-weight library that any Python developer who wants to work with LLMs and agents (whether simple or complex) should feel no hesitation to pull into their project. It's not meant to be everything to everyone, but it should enable people to build just about anything.

As such, we prefer strong primitives, powerful abstractions, and general solutions and extension points that enable people to build things that we hadn't even thought of, over narrow solutions for specific use cases, opinionated solutions that push a particular approach to agent design that hasn't yet stood the test of time, or generally "every single possible battery included" solutions that make the library unnecessarily bloated. This preference is about shaping designs, new public APIs, and extension points -- it is not a license to widen a bug fix beyond the defect you reproduced (see "Requirements of all contributions").

# Requirements of all contributions

All changes need to:

- be thoughtful and deliberate about new abstractions, public APIs, and behaviors, as every wrong-in-retrospect choice (made in a rush or with insufficient context) makes life harder for hundreds of thousands of users (and agents), and is much more difficult to change later than to do right the first time
- be scoped to the problem you are solving: for a bug fix, make the narrowest change that resolves the reported, reproduced behavior -- often one line plus one regression test -- and stop. The preference for general primitives and powerful abstractions (see Philosophy) is for shaping designs and new public surface, not for widening a bug fix. Extend a fix to sibling fields, providers, or models only after confirming, by reproducing, that they share the same defect; an "others might also be affected" *hunch* is unacceptable: if a concern is verified, it can be included in the same PR if it doesn't explode scope or delays an already mergeable PR, otherwise it should be filed as an issue with enough context and guidance for someone to file a PR for it. Do not refactor a shared protocol, helper, or abstraction to fix one caller unless the narrow fix is unavailable or the refactor is itself the confirmed fix
- be backward compatible as laid out in the [version policy](docs/version-policy.md), so that users can upgrade with confidence
- be fully type-safe (both internally and in public API) without unnecessary `cast`s or `Any`s, so that users don't need `isinstance` checks and can trust that code that typechecks will work at runtime
- have comprehensive tests covering 100% of code paths, favoring integration tests and real requests (using recordings and snapshots -- see below) over unit tests and mocking
- update/add all relevant documentation, following the existing voice and patterns
- update the relevant agent skills when introducing a new feature or when a skill needs to reflect the correct mechanics; Pydantic AI skills belong in [pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/.agents/skills/building-pydantic-ai-agents/](pydantic_ai_slim/pydantic_ai/.agents/skills/building-pydantic-ai-agents/), while repository workflow skills live under [.claude/skills/](.claude/skills/)

When you submit a PR, make sure you include the [PR template](.github/pull_request_template.md) and fill in the issue number that should be closed when the PR is merged. The "AI generated code" checkbox should always be checked manually by the user in the UI, not by the agent.

PR titles feed directly into the release changelog — wrap code identifiers (class names, keyword arguments, module paths, CLI flags, env vars) in backticks, matching the style of recent release notes (e.g. `git log main --oneline -10`).

Never add yourself (Claude) as a co-author on commits. Commits should be authored as the user only, with no `Co-Authored-By` trailer referencing Claude.

## Repository structure

The repo contains a `uv` workspace defining multiple Python packages:

- `pydantic-ai-slim` in `pydantic_ai_slim/`: the [agent framework](docs/agent.md), including the `Agent` class and `Model` classes for each model provider/API
    - This is a slim package with minimal dependencies and optional dependency groups for each model provider (e.g. `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`) or integration (e.g. `logfire`, `mcp`, `temporal`).
- `pydantic-graph` in `pydantic_graph/`: the type-hint based [graph library](docs/graph.md) that powers the agent loop
- `pydantic-evals` in `pydantic_evals/`: the [evaluation framework](docs/evals.md) for evaluating the arbitrary stochastic functions including LLMs and agents
- `clai` in `clai/`: a [CLI](docs/cli.md) (with an optional [web UI](docs/web.md)) to chat with Pydantic AI agents
- `pydantic-ai` defined in `pyproject.toml` at the root, bringing in the packages above as well the optional dependency groups for all model providers and select integrations.

## Development workflow

The project uses:

- [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), supporting Python 3.10 through 3.13
    - Install all dependencies with `make install`
- `pre-commit`, can be installed with `uv tool install pre-commit`
- `ruff` via `make lint` and `make format`
- `pyright` via `make typecheck`
- `pytest` in `tests/`, via `make test`, with:
    - `inline-snapshot` for inline assertions
    - `pytest-recording` and `vcrpy` for recording and playing back requests to model APIs
- `mkdocs` in `docs/`, via `make docs` and `make docs-serve`, served at <https://ai.pydantic.dev>, with:
    - `mkdocstrings-python` to generate API docs from docstrings and types
    - `mkdocs-material` to theme the docs
    - `tests/test_examples.py` to test all code examples in the docs (including docstrings)
- [`logfire`](docs/logfire.md) for OTel instrumentation of Pydantic AI and `httpx`
    - If you have access to the Logfire MCP server, you can use it to inspect agent runs, tool calls, and model requests

## When to verify

Pre-commit runs `make lint`, `make format`, and `make typecheck` automatically on every commit; CI additionally runs the full test suite. While iterating, only run targeted checks on the files/tests you have a specific reason to suspect:

- typecheck a single file: `PYRIGHT_PYTHON_IGNORE_WARNINGS=1 uv run pyright path/to/file.py`
- run a single test: `uv run pytest path/to/test.py::test_name`

Avoid `make typecheck` and `make test` between edits — both are slow and the pre-commit/CI gates cover them at the right time.

188:         self,

190:         """Provide async-iteration over the nodes in the agent run."""
191:         if self.ctx.deps.root_capability.has_wrap_node_run:

194:                 'does not fire them. Use `agent_run.next(node)` to advance the run, or use '
195:                 '`agent.run()` which drives via `next()` automatically.',
196:                 UserWarning,

201:     async def __anext__(
202:         self,
203:     ) -> _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, OutputDataT] | End[FinalResult[OutputDataT]]:
204:         """Advance to the next node automatically based on the last returned node.
205: 
206:         Note: this uses the graph run's internal iteration which does NOT call
207:         node hooks (`before_node_run`, `wrap_node_run`, `after_node_run`,
208:         `on_node_run_error`). Use `next()` for capability-hooked iteration, or
209:         use `agent.run()` which drives via `next()` automatically.
210:         """
211:         if self._result_override is not None:
212:             raise StopAsyncIteration
213:         try:
214:             task = await anext(self._graph_run)
215:         except BaseException as exc:
216:             self._node_error = exc
217:             raise
218:         node = self._task_to_node(task)
219:         if isinstance(node, End) and self._graph_run.state.pending_messages:
220:             # `asap` messages drain in `before_model_request` (which fires either way), but
221:             # `when_idle` messages and end-of-run redirects drain in `after_node_run`, which
222:             # bare iteration skips. Reaching `End` with a non-empty queue means those were
223:             # stranded — fail loudly rather than silently dropping the messages.
224:             raise exceptions.UndrainedPendingMessagesError(
225:                 'The agent run ended with undrained pending messages enqueued via `enqueue`. '
226:                 'Bare `async for node in agent_run` does not drain `when_idle` messages or '
227:                 'end-of-run redirects, because they fire in `after_node_run`, which bare iteration '
228:                 'skips. Use `agent_run.next(node)` to advance the run, or `agent.run()` which drives '
229:                 'via `next()` automatically.'
230:             )
231:         return node
232: 
233:     def _task_to_node(
234:         self, task: EndMarker[FinalResult[OutputDataT]] | JoinItem | Sequence[GraphTaskRequest]
235:     ) -> _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, OutputDataT] | End[FinalResult[OutputDataT]]:
236:         if isinstance(task, Sequence) and len(task) == 1:
237:             first_task = task[0]
238:             if isinstance(first_task.inputs, BaseNode):  # pragma: no branch
239:                 base_node: BaseNode[  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownVariableType]
240:                     _agent_graph.GraphAgentState,
241:                     _agent_graph.GraphAgentDeps[AgentDepsT, OutputDataT],
242:                     FinalResult[OutputDataT],
243:                 ] = first_task.inputs  # pyright: ignore[reportUnknownMemberType]
244:                 if _agent_graph.is_agent_node(node=base_node):  # pragma: no branch
245:                     return base_node
246:         if isinstance(task, EndMarker):
247:             return End(task.value)
248:         raise exceptions.AgentRunError(f'Unexpected node: {task}')  # pragma: no cover
249: 
250:     def _node_to_task(self, node: _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, OutputDataT]) -> GraphTaskRequest:
251:         return GraphTaskRequest(NodeStep(type(node)).id, inputs=node, fork_stack=())
252: 
253:     def _sync_graph_state(self, result: _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any] | End[FinalResult[Any]]) -> None:
254:         """Synchronize the graph runner's state to match a hook-modified result.
255: 
256:         After a capability hook changes the result (e.g. `on_node_run_error` recovering,
257:         or `after_node_run` converting End↔node), the graph runner's internal `_next` must
258:         be updated so that `output` and `next_node` reflect the hook's decision.
259:         """
260:         if isinstance(result, End):
261:             self._graph_run.override_next(EndMarker(result.data))
262:         else:
263:             self._graph_run.override_next([self._node_to_task(result)])
264: 
265:     async def _advance_graph(
266:         self,
267:         node: _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any],
268:     ) -> _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any] | End[FinalResult[Any]]:
269:         """Execute a single graph step without firing capability hooks."""
270:         task = [self._node_to_task(node)]
271:         try:
272:             task = await self._graph_run.next(task)
273:         except StopAsyncIteration:
274:             pass
275:         return self._task_to_node(task)
276: 
277:     async def _wrap_and_advance(
278:         self,
279:         run_context: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
280:         node: _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any],
281:         step_fn: Callable[
282:             [_agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any]],
283:             Awaitable[_agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any] | End[FinalResult[Any]]],
284:         ],
285:     ) -> _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any] | End[FinalResult[Any]]:
286:         """Execute `wrap_node_run(step_fn)` → `on_node_run_error` → `after_node_run`.
287: 
288:         This is the portion of the hook lifecycle after `before_node_run` has already fired.
289:         Used by both `_run_node_with_hooks` and directly by `run_stream()` which calls
290:         `before_node_run` separately (before streaming).
291:         """
292:         cap = self.ctx.deps.root_capability
293:         try:
294:             result = await cap.wrap_node_run(run_context, node=node, handler=step_fn)
295:         except Exception as e:
296:             result = await cap.on_node_run_error(run_context, node=node, error=e)
297:             # on_node_run_error recovered by returning a result.
298:             # The graph runner is in ErrorMarker state; update it to match.
299:             self._sync_graph_state(result)
300:         pre_hook_result = result
301:         result = await cap.after_node_run(run_context, node=node, result=result)
302: 
303:         # If after_node_run changed the result, sync the graph runner state so
304:         # agent_run.result correctly reflects whether the run is finished.
305:         if result is not pre_hook_result:
306:             self._sync_graph_state(result)
307: 
308:         return result
309: 
310:     async def _run_node_with_hooks(
311:         self,
312:         node: _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any],
313:         step_fn: Callable[
314:             [_agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any]],
315:             Awaitable[_agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any] | End[FinalResult[Any]]],
316:         ],
317:     ) -> _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, Any] | End[FinalResult[Any]]:
318:         """Run a node through the full capability hook lifecycle with a custom step function.
319: 
320:         Fires hooks in order: `before_node_run` → `wrap_node_run(step_fn)` → `after_node_run`,
321:         with `on_node_run_error` handling exceptions from `wrap_node_run`.
322:         """
323:         run_context = _agent_graph.build_run_context(self.ctx)
324:         cap = self.ctx.deps.root_capability
325:         node = await cap.before_node_run(run_context, node=node)
326:         return await self._wrap_and_advance(run_context, node, step_fn)

328:     async def next(
329:         self,
330:         node: _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, OutputDataT],
331:     ) -> _agent_graph.AgentNode[AgentDepsT, OutputDataT] | End[FinalResult[OutputDataT]]:
332:         """Manually drive the agent run by passing in the node you want to run next.
333: 
334:         This lets you inspect or mutate the node before continuing execution, or skip certain nodes
335:         under dynamic conditions. The agent run should be stopped when you return an [`End`][pydantic_graph.basenode.End]
336:         node.
337: 
338:         Example:
339:         ```python
340:         from pydantic_ai import Agent
341:         from pydantic_graph import End
342: 
343:         agent = Agent('openai:gpt-5.2')
344: 
345:         async def main():
346:             async with agent.iter('What is the capital of France?') as agent_run:
347:                 next_node = agent_run.next_node  # start with the first node
348:                 nodes = [next_node]
349:                 while not isinstance(next_node, End):
350:                     next_node = await agent_run.next(next_node)
351:                     nodes.append(next_node)
352:                 # Once `next_node` is an End, we've finished:
353:                 print(nodes)
354:                 '''
355:                 [
356:                     UserPromptNode(
357:                         user_prompt='What is the capital of France?',
358:                         instructions_functions=[],
359:                         system_prompts=(),
360:                         system_prompt_functions=[],
361:                         system_prompt_dynamic_functions={},
362:                     ),
363:                     ModelRequestNode(
364:                         request=ModelRequest(
365:                             parts=[
366:                                 UserPromptPart(
367:                                     content='What is the capital of France?',
368:                                     timestamp=datetime.datetime(...),
369:                                 )
370:                             ],
371:                             timestamp=datetime.datetime(...),
372:                             run_id='...',
373:                             conversation_id='...',
374:                         )
375:                     ),
376:                     CallToolsNode(
377:                         model_response=ModelResponse(
378:                             parts=[TextPart(content='The capital of France is Paris.')],
379:                             usage=RequestUsage(input_tokens=56, output_tokens=7),
380:                             model_name='gpt-5.2',
381:                             timestamp=datetime.datetime(...),
382:                             run_id='...',
383:                             conversation_id='...',
384:                         )
385:                     ),
386:                     End(data=FinalResult(output='The capital of France is Paris.')),
387:                 ]
388:                 '''
389:                 print('Final result:', agent_run.result.output)
390:                 #> Final result: The capital of France is Paris.
391:         ```
392: 
393:         Args:
394:             node: The node to run next in the graph.
395: 
396:         Returns:
397:             The next node returned by the graph logic, or an [`End`][pydantic_graph.basenode.End] node if
398:             the run has completed.
399:         """
400:         # Note: It might be nice to expose a synchronous interface for iteration, but we shouldn't do it
401:         # on this class, or else IDEs won't warn you if you accidentally use `for` instead of `async for` to iterate.
402:         return await self._run_node_with_hooks(node, self._advance_graph)

413:

416:         """The unique identifier for the agent run."""
417:         return self._graph_run.state.run_id
418:

427: 
428:         Exposed for inspection / debugging; use [`enqueue`][pydantic_ai.run.AgentRun.enqueue] to add messages.
429:         """

432:     def enqueue(
433:         self,
434:         *content: EnqueueContent,
435:         priority: PendingMessagePriority = 'asap',
436:     ) -> None:
437:         """Enqueue content to be injected into the conversation.
438: 
439:         Designed to be called from the same event loop driving `agent.iter()`. If
440:         you're forwarding events from a different thread (e.g. a webhook handler
441:         running on its own loop or thread), marshal the call back onto the agent's
442:         loop first (e.g. `loop.call_soon_threadsafe(agent_run.enqueue, msg)`).

1. **`run_id` ≠ `conversation_id`** (independent IDs) — my `AgentRunData` should carry both, and `objectiveId` for cross-run intent.
2. **`GraphAgentState`** is the resumable checkpoint — directly maps to my `checkpointJson`, but it's a *first-class, versioned* state object, not opaque JSON. I should make checkpoint a typed, time-travelable state node.

4. **`usage.RunUsage` / `UsageLimits`** — cost is a *first-class, accruing, limit-checked* resource, not a passive `costJson`. Durable exec (Temporal/DBOS/Prefect) is the "long-running multi-provider" pattern — I need a `DurableCheckpoint` concept.
5. **Capabilities as composable middleware** (`before_model_request`, `wrap_node_run`, `after_node_run`, `on_node_run_error`) — governance/limits/policy should be *capabilities* applied to runs, not hardcoded. This is the "do anything n8n can do" extensibility model.
6. **`enqueue` / pending messages / `when_idle` vs `asap`** — agents can inject tasks mid-run; maps to my Objective Agenda + a mid-run inbox.
7. **Dynamic toolsets (`for_run_step`, tool search, deferred loading)** — tools are discovered/loaded per step; maps to `cap-store.tool` + a `Toolset` binding.

292:         model calls the `load_capability` tool for this capability.
293:         """
294:         return None
295: 
296:     def get_toolset(self) -> AgentToolset[AgentDepsT] | None:
297:         """Return a toolset to register with the agent, or None."""
298:         return None
299: 
300:     def get_native_tools(self) -> Sequence[AgentNativeTool[AgentDepsT]]:
301:         """Return native tools to register with the agent."""
302:         return []
303: 
304:     def get_wrapper_toolset(self, toolset: AbstractToolset[AgentDepsT]) -> AbstractToolset[AgentDepsT] | None:
305:         """Wrap the agent's assembled toolset, or return None to leave it unchanged.
306: 
307:         Called per-run with the combined non-output toolset (after the
308:         [`prepare_tools`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.prepare_tools] hook
309:         has already wrapped it). Output tools are added separately and are not included.
310: 
311:         Unlike value-contribution methods such as
312:         [`get_instructions`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.get_instructions],
313:         this receives the already assembled toolset and is called each run (after
314:         [`for_run`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.for_run]).
315:         When multiple capabilities provide wrappers, they follow middleware semantics:
316:         the first capability in the list wraps outermost (matching `wrap_*` hooks).
317: 
318:         Use this to apply cross-cutting toolset wrappers like
319:         [`PreparedToolset`][pydantic_ai.toolsets.PreparedToolset],
320:         [`FilteredToolset`][pydantic_ai.toolsets.FilteredToolset],
321:         or custom [`WrapperToolset`][pydantic_ai.toolsets.WrapperToolset] subclasses.
322:         """
323:         return None
324: 
325:     # --- Tool preparation hooks ---
326: 
327:     async def prepare_tools(
328:         self,
329:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
330:         tool_defs: list[ToolDefinition],
331:     ) -> list[ToolDefinition]:
332:         """Filter or modify function tool definitions for this step.
333: 
334:         Receives **function** tools only. For [output tools][pydantic_ai.output.ToolOutput],
335:         override
336:         [`prepare_output_tools`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.prepare_output_tools]
337:         — it runs separately, with `ctx.retry`/`ctx.max_retries` reflecting the **output**
338:         retry budget instead of the function-tool budget.
339: 
340:         Return a filtered or modified list. The result flows into both the model's request
341:         parameters and `ToolManager.tools`, so filtering also blocks tool execution.
342:         """
343:         return tool_defs
344: 
345:     async def prepare_output_tools(
346:         self,
347:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
348:         tool_defs: list[ToolDefinition],
349:     ) -> list[ToolDefinition]:
350:         """Filter or modify output tool definitions for this step.
351: 
352:         Receives only [output tools][pydantic_ai.output.ToolOutput]. `ctx.retry` and
353:         `ctx.max_retries` reflect the **output** retry budget (agent-level
354:         `max_output_retries`), matching the output hook lifecycle.
355: 
356:         Return a filtered or modified list. The result flows into both the model's request
357:         parameters and `ToolManager.tools`, so filtering also blocks tool execution.
358:         """
359:         return tool_defs
360: 
361:     # --- Run lifecycle hooks ---
362: 
363:     async def before_run(
364:         self,
365:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
366:     ) -> None:
367:         """Called before the agent run starts. Observe-only; use wrap_run for modification."""
368: 
369:     async def after_run(
370:         self,
371:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
372:         *,
373:         result: AgentRunResult[Any],
374:     ) -> AgentRunResult[Any]:
375:         """Called after the agent run completes. Can modify the result."""
376:         return result
377: 
378:     async def wrap_run(
379:         self,
380:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
381:         *,
382:         handler: WrapRunHandler,
383:     ) -> AgentRunResult[Any]:
384:         """Wraps the entire agent run. `handler()` executes the run.
385: 
386:         If `handler()` raises and this method catches the exception and
387:         returns a result instead, the error is suppressed and the recovery
388:         result is used.
389: 
390:         If this method does not call `handler()` (short-circuit), the run
391:         is skipped and the returned result is used directly.
392: 
393:         Note: if the caller cancels the run (e.g. by breaking out of an
394:         `iter()` loop), this method receives an `asyncio.CancelledError`.
395:         Implementations that hold resources should handle cleanup accordingly.
396:         """
397:         return await handler()
398: 
399:     async def on_run_error(
400:         self,
401:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
402:         *,
403:         error: BaseException,
404:     ) -> AgentRunResult[Any]:
405:         """Called when the agent run fails with an exception.
406: 
407:         This is the error counterpart to
408:         [`after_run`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_run]:
409:         while `after_run` is called on success, `on_run_error` is called on
410:         failure (after [`wrap_run`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.wrap_run]
411:         has had its chance to recover).
412: 
413:         **Raise** the original `error` (or a different exception) to propagate it.
414:         **Return** an [`AgentRunResult`][pydantic_ai.run.AgentRunResult] to suppress
415:         the error and recover the run.
416: 
417:         Not called for `GeneratorExit` or `KeyboardInterrupt`.
418:         """
419:         raise error
420: 
421:     # --- Node run lifecycle hooks ---
422: 
423:     async def before_node_run(
424:         self,
425:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
426:         *,
427:         node: AgentNode[AgentDepsT],
428:     ) -> AgentNode[AgentDepsT]:
429:         """Called before each graph node executes. Can observe or replace the node."""
430:         return node
431: 
432:     async def after_node_run(
433:         self,
434:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
435:         *,
436:         node: AgentNode[AgentDepsT],
437:         result: NodeResult[AgentDepsT],
438:     ) -> NodeResult[AgentDepsT]:
439:         """Called after each graph node succeeds. Can modify the result (next node or `End`)."""
440:         return result
441: 
442:     async def wrap_node_run(
443:         self,
444:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
445:         *,
446:         node: AgentNode[AgentDepsT],
447:         handler: WrapNodeRunHandler[AgentDepsT],
448:     ) -> NodeResult[AgentDepsT]:
449:         """Wraps execution of each agent graph node (run step).
450: 
451:         Called for every node in the agent graph (`UserPromptNode`,
452:         `ModelRequestNode`, `CallToolsNode`).  `handler(node)` executes
453:         the node and returns the next node (or `End`).
454: 
455:         Override to inspect or modify nodes before execution, inspect or modify
456:         the returned next node, call `handler` multiple times (retry), or
457:         return a different node to redirect graph progression.
458: 
459:         Note: this hook fires when using `agent.run()`,
460:         `agent.run_stream()`, and when manually driving
461:         an `agent.iter()` run with `agent_run.next()`, but it does **not** fire when
462:         iterating over the run with bare `async for` (which yields stream events, not
463:         node results).
464: 
465:         When using `agent.run()` with `event_stream_handler`, the handler wraps both
466:         streaming and graph advancement (i.e. the model call happens inside the wrapper).
467:         When using `agent.run_stream()`, the handler wraps only graph advancement — streaming
468:         happens before the wrapper because `run_stream()` must yield the stream to the caller
469:         while the stream context is still open, which cannot happen from inside a callback.
470:         """
471:         return await handler(node)
472: 
473:     async def on_node_run_error(
474:         self,
475:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
476:         *,
477:         node: AgentNode[AgentDepsT],
478:         error: Exception,
479:     ) -> NodeResult[AgentDepsT]:
480:         """Called when a graph node fails with an exception.
481: 
482:         This is the error counterpart to
483:         [`after_node_run`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_node_run].
484: 
485:         **Raise** the original `error` (or a different exception) to propagate it.
486:         **Return** a next node or `End` to recover and continue the graph.
487: 
488:         Useful for recovering from
489:         [`UnexpectedModelBehavior`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.UnexpectedModelBehavior]
490:         by redirecting to a different node (e.g. retry with different model settings).
491:         """
492:         raise error
493: 
494:     # --- Event stream hook ---
495: 
496:     async def wrap_run_event_stream(
497:         self,
498:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
499:         *,
500:         stream: AsyncIterable[AgentStreamEvent],
501:     ) -> AsyncIterable[AgentStreamEvent]:
502:         """Wraps the event stream for a streamed node. Can observe or transform events.
503: 
504:         Note: when this method is overridden (or [`Hooks.on.event`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.hooks.Hooks.on]
505:         / [`Hooks.on.run_event_stream`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.hooks.Hooks.on] are registered),
506:         `agent.run()` automatically enables streaming mode so this hook
507:         fires even without an explicit `event_stream_handler`.
508:         """
509:         async for event in stream:
510:             yield event
511: 
512:     # --- Model request lifecycle hooks ---
513: 
514:     async def before_model_request(
515:         self,
516:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
517:         request_context: ModelRequestContext,
518:     ) -> ModelRequestContext:
519:         """Called before each model request. Can modify messages, settings, and parameters."""
520:         return request_context
521: 
522:     async def after_model_request(
523:         self,
524:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
525:         *,
526:         request_context: ModelRequestContext,
527:         response: ModelResponse,
528:     ) -> ModelResponse:
529:         """Called after each model response. Can modify the response before further processing.
530: 
531:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to reject the response and
532:         ask the model to try again. The original response is still appended to message history
533:         so the model can see what it said. Retries count against the output side of the agent's retry budget.
534:         """
535:         return response
536: 
537:     async def wrap_model_request(
538:         self,
539:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
540:         *,
541:         request_context: ModelRequestContext,
542:         handler: WrapModelRequestHandler,
543:     ) -> ModelResponse:
544:         """Wraps the model request. handler() calls the model.
545: 
546:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to skip `on_model_request_error`
547:         and directly retry the model request with a retry prompt. If the handler was called,
548:         the model response is preserved in history for context (same as `after_model_request`).
549:         """
550:         return await handler(request_context)
551: 
552:     async def on_model_request_error(
553:         self,
554:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
555:         *,
556:         request_context: ModelRequestContext,
557:         error: Exception,
558:     ) -> ModelResponse:
559:         """Called when a model request fails with an exception.
560: 
561:         This is the error counterpart to
562:         [`after_model_request`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_model_request].
563: 
564:         **Raise** the original `error` (or a different exception) to propagate it.
565:         **Return** a [`ModelResponse`][pydantic_ai.messages.ModelResponse] to suppress
566:         the error and use the response as if the model call succeeded.
567:         **Raise** [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to retry the model request
568:         with a retry prompt instead of recovering or propagating.
569: 
570:         Not called for [`SkipModelRequest`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.SkipModelRequest]
571:         or [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry].
572:         """
573:         raise error
574: 
575:     # --- Tool validate lifecycle hooks ---
576: 
577:     async def before_tool_validate(
578:         self,
579:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
580:         *,
581:         call: ToolCallPart,
582:         tool_def: ToolDefinition,
583:         args: RawToolArgs,
584:     ) -> RawToolArgs:
585:         """Modify raw args before validation.
586: 
587:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to skip validation and
588:         ask the model to redo the tool call.
589:         """
590:         return args
591: 
592:     async def after_tool_validate(
593:         self,
594:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
595:         *,
596:         call: ToolCallPart,
597:         tool_def: ToolDefinition,
598:         args: ValidatedToolArgs,
599:     ) -> ValidatedToolArgs:
600:         """Modify validated args. Called only on successful validation.
601: 
602:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to reject the validated args
603:         and ask the model to redo the tool call.
604:         """
605:         return args
606: 
607:     async def wrap_tool_validate(
608:         self,
609:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
610:         *,
611:         call: ToolCallPart,
612:         tool_def: ToolDefinition,
613:         args: RawToolArgs,
614:         handler: WrapToolValidateHandler,
615:     ) -> ValidatedToolArgs:
616:         """Wraps tool argument validation. handler() runs the validation."""
617:         return await handler(args)
618: 
619:     async def on_tool_validate_error(
620:         self,
621:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
622:         *,
623:         call: ToolCallPart,
624:         tool_def: ToolDefinition,
625:         args: RawToolArgs,
626:         error: ValidationError | ModelRetry,
627:     ) -> ValidatedToolArgs:
628:         """Called when tool argument validation fails.
629: 
630:         This is the error counterpart to
631:         [`after_tool_validate`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_tool_validate].
632:         Fires for `ValidationError` (schema mismatch) and
633:         [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] (custom validator rejection).
634: 
635:         **Raise** the original `error` (or a different exception) to propagate it.
636:         **Return** validated args to suppress the error and continue as if validation passed.
637: 
638:         Not called for [`SkipToolValidation`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.SkipToolValidation].
639:         """
640:         raise error
641: 
642:     # --- Tool execute lifecycle hooks ---
643: 
644:     async def before_tool_execute(
645:         self,
646:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
647:         *,
648:         call: ToolCallPart,
649:         tool_def: ToolDefinition,
650:         args: ValidatedToolArgs,
651:     ) -> ValidatedToolArgs:
652:         """Modify validated args before execution.
653: 
654:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to skip execution and
655:         ask the model to redo the tool call.
656:         """
657:         return args
658: 
659:     async def after_tool_execute(
660:         self,
661:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
662:         *,
663:         call: ToolCallPart,
664:         tool_def: ToolDefinition,
665:         args: ValidatedToolArgs,
666:         result: Any,
667:     ) -> Any:
668:         """Modify result after execution.
669: 
670:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to reject the tool result
671:         and ask the model to redo the tool call.
672:         """
673:         return result
674: 
675:     async def wrap_tool_execute(
676:         self,
677:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
678:         *,
679:         call: ToolCallPart,
680:         tool_def: ToolDefinition,
681:         args: ValidatedToolArgs,
682:         handler: WrapToolExecuteHandler,
683:     ) -> Any:
684:         """Wraps tool execution. handler() runs the tool."""
685:         return await handler(args)
686: 
687:     async def on_tool_execute_error(
688:         self,
689:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
690:         *,
691:         call: ToolCallPart,
692:         tool_def: ToolDefinition,
693:         args: ValidatedToolArgs,
694:         error: Exception,
695:     ) -> Any:
696:         """Called when tool execution fails with an exception.
697: 
698:         This is the error counterpart to
699:         [`after_tool_execute`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_tool_execute].
700: 
701:         **Raise** the original `error` (or a different exception) to propagate it.
702:         **Return** any value to suppress the error and use it as the tool result.
703:         **Raise** [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to ask the model to
704:         redo the tool call instead of recovering or propagating.
705: 
706:         Not called for control flow exceptions
707:         ([`SkipToolExecution`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.SkipToolExecution],
708:         [`CallDeferred`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.CallDeferred],
709:         [`ApprovalRequired`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ApprovalRequired])
710:         or retry signals ([`ToolRetryError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ToolRetryError]
711:         from [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry]).
712:         Use [`wrap_tool_execute`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.wrap_tool_execute]
713:         to intercept retries.
714:         """
715:         raise error
716: 
717:     # --- Output validate lifecycle hooks ---
718: 
719:     async def before_output_validate(
720:         self,
721:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
722:         *,
723:         output_context: OutputContext,
724:         output: RawOutput,
725:     ) -> RawOutput:
726:         """Modify raw model output before validation/parsing.
727: 
728:         The primary hook for pre-parse repair and normalization of model output.
729:         Fires only for structured output that requires parsing: prompted, native,
730:         tool, and union output. Does **not** fire for plain text or image output.
731: 
732:         For structured text output, `output` is the raw text string from the model.
733:         For tool output, `output` is the raw tool arguments (string or dict).
734: 
735:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to skip validation and
736:         ask the model to try again with a custom message.
737: 
738:         During streaming, this hook fires on every partial validation attempt as well as
739:         the final result. Check `ctx.partial_output` to distinguish and avoid expensive
740:         work on partial results.
741:         """
742:         return output
743: 
744:     async def after_output_validate(
745:         self,
746:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
747:         *,
748:         output_context: OutputContext,
749:         output: Any,
750:     ) -> Any:
751:         """Modify validated output after successful parsing. Called only on success.
752: 
753:         `output` is the **semantic value** the model was asked to produce — e.g., a
754:         `MyModel` instance for `output_type=MyModel`, or `42` for `output_type=int`, or
755:         the input to a single-arg output function. For multi-arg output functions, this
756:         is the `dict` of arguments (the genuine multi-value input).
757: 
758:         Note: this differs from *tool* hooks (`after_tool_validate`), which always see
759:         `dict[str, Any]` — tool args follow the schema contract. Output hooks see the
760:         semantic output value, regardless of how it's internally represented during
761:         validation.
762: 
763:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to reject the validated
764:         output and ask the model to try again.
765:         """
766:         return output
767: 
768:     async def wrap_output_validate(
769:         self,
770:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
771:         *,
772:         output_context: OutputContext,
773:         output: RawOutput,
774:         handler: WrapOutputValidateHandler,
775:     ) -> Any:
776:         """Wraps output validation. handler(output) performs the validation.
777: 
778:         [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] from within the handler goes to
779:         [`on_output_validate_error`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.on_output_validate_error].
780:         `ModelRetry` raised directly (not from the handler) bypasses the error hook.
781:         """
782:         return await handler(output)
783: 
784:     async def on_output_validate_error(
785:         self,
786:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
787:         *,
788:         output_context: OutputContext,
789:         output: RawOutput,
790:         error: ValidationError | ModelRetry,
791:     ) -> Any:
792:         """Called when output validation fails.
793: 
794:         This is the error counterpart to
795:         [`after_output_validate`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_output_validate].
796: 
797:         **Raise** the original `error` (or a different exception) to propagate it.
798:         **Return** validated output to suppress the error and continue.
799:         """
800:         raise error
801: 
802:     # --- Output process lifecycle hooks ---
803: 
804:     async def before_output_process(
805:         self,
806:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
807:         *,
808:         output_context: OutputContext,
809:         output: Any,
810:     ) -> Any:
811:         """Modify validated output before processing (extraction, output function call).
812: 
813:         `output` is the **semantic value** — e.g., a `MyModel` instance or `42`, matching
814:         `after_output_validate`. For multi-arg output functions, it's the `dict` of args.
815:         See [`after_output_validate`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_output_validate]
816:         for a full explanation of the semantic-value contract.
817: 
818:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to skip processing and
819:         ask the model to try again.
820:         """
821:         return output
822: 
823:     async def after_output_process(
824:         self,
825:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
826:         *,
827:         output_context: OutputContext,
828:         output: Any,
829:     ) -> Any:
830:         """Modify result after output processing.
831: 
832:         Raise [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] to reject the result
833:         and ask the model to try again.
834:         """
835:         return output
836: 
837:     async def wrap_output_process(
838:         self,
839:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
840:         *,
841:         output_context: OutputContext,
842:         output: Any,
843:         handler: WrapOutputProcessHandler,
844:     ) -> Any:
845:         """Wraps output processing. handler(output) runs extraction + output function call.
846: 
847:         [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry] bypasses
848:         [`on_output_process_error`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.on_output_process_error]
849:         (treated as control flow, not an error).
850: 
851:         During streaming, this fires only when partial validation succeeds, and on the
852:         final result. Check `ctx.partial_output` to skip expensive work on partial results.
853:         """
854:         return await handler(output)
855: 
856:     async def on_output_process_error(
857:         self,
858:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
859:         *,
860:         output_context: OutputContext,
861:         output: Any,
862:         error: Exception,
863:     ) -> Any:
864:         """Called when output processing fails with an exception.
865: 
866:         This is the error counterpart to
867:         [`after_output_process`][pydantic_ai.capabilities.AbstractCapability.after_output_process].
868: 
869:         **Raise** the original `error` (or a different exception) to propagate it.
870:         **Return** any value to suppress the error and use it as the output.
871: 
872:         Not called for retry signals ([`ToolRetryError`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ToolRetryError]
873:         from [`ModelRetry`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ModelRetry]).
874:         """
875:         raise error
876: 
877:     # --- Deferred tool call hooks ---
878: 
879:     async def handle_deferred_tool_calls(
880:         self,
881:         ctx: RunContext[AgentDepsT],
882:         *,
883:         requests: DeferredToolRequests,
884:     ) -> DeferredToolResults | None:
885:         """Handle deferred tool calls (approval-required or externally-executed) inline during an agent run.
886: 
887:         Called by `ToolManager` when:
888: 
889:         - a tool raises [`ApprovalRequired`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.ApprovalRequired] or
890:           [`CallDeferred`][pydantic_ai.exceptions.CallDeferred] during execution, or
891:         - the model calls a tool registered with `requires_approval=True` (see
892:           [Human-in-the-Loop Tool Approval](../deferred-tools.md#human-in-the-loop-tool-approval))
893:           or a tool backed by [external execution](../deferred-tools.md#external-tool-execution).
894: 
895:         Uses accumulation dispatch: each capability in the chain receives remaining
896:         unresolved requests and can resolve some or all of them. Results are merged
897:         and unresolved calls are passed to the next capability.
898:

# capabilities/ Guidelines

Capabilities are the composable home for cross-cutting agent behavior.

- Prefer a capability over a new `Agent` constructor kwarg when behavior contributes instructions, settings, tools, native tools, wrappers, lifecycle hooks, or event/history processing.
- Keep capabilities provider-agnostic unless the capability is explicitly modeling a provider-native feature; provider-specific facts belong in providers/profiles or provider-native tool classes.
- Preserve composition order. If a capability wraps model/tool/output/event behavior, check how it interacts with `CombinedCapability` and adjacent capabilities.
- For user-facing capabilities, update docs and examples so users discover the capability as the primary API, not an implementation detail.
- Check durable execution, agent specs, and serialized configuration before adding non-serializable state or hidden runtime dependencies.

262:     The request count is tracked by pydantic_ai, and the request limit is checked before each request to the model.

272:     input_tokens_limit: int | None = None
273:     """The maximum number of input/prompt tokens allowed."""
274:     output_tokens_limit: int | None = None

277:     """The maximum number of tokens allowed in requests and responses combined."""

280:     to enforce `input_tokens_limit` ahead of time.

283:     and is disabled by default.

286:

288:     - Google
289:     - Bedrock Converse
290:     - OpenAI Responses
291:     """
292: 
293:     def has_token_limits(self) -> bool:

299:         If there are no limits, we can skip that processing in the streaming response iterator.

301:         return any(

303:         )

306:         """Raises a `UsageLimitExceeded` exception if the next request would exceed any of the limits."""
307:         request_limit = self.request_limit
308:         if request_limit is not None and usage.requests >= request_limit:
309:             raise UsageLimitExceeded(f'The next request would exceed the request_limit of {request_limit}')

4. **`end_strategy` (early/graceful/exhaustive)** — a governance/policy field for parallel tool+output handling.
5. **Durable execution** (Temporal/DBOS/Prefect) — long-running runs are *checkpointable across process boundaries*; `AgentRun` state must be a serializable, resumable object, not in-memory only.

7. **Deferred / approval-required tools** → `tool_call` can be `pending_human` → ties to HITL gates.
8. **Dynamic toolsets (`for_run_step`, tool search, deferred loading)** → `cap-store.tool` is discovered/loaded per step; toolsets are bindings.

Never overload them.\n- **Cost is a first-class, limit-checked resource**: `RunBudget` accrues and enforces\n  `UsageLimits` (request/tool/token ceilings) — raises `BudgetExceededError` before/after calls.\n- **Durable by default**: `AgentRunData.checkpointJson` + `RunInbox` + `cap-store.capability.configJson`\n  are all serializable (no runtime closures) so runs resume across process restarts (Temporal/DBOS-style).\n- **Compose with existing**: `RouteSpec`/`RouteTarget` = transport under `governance_policy`\n  (policy: role→agent; route: agent→provider/account). `Workflow*` = n8n DAGs whose nodes can\n  reference `cap-store.agent_run` / `cap-store.tool` by node id. `UiComponent` hot-swap binds via\n  `SlotBinding` (audited).\n\n## 4. Storage Contracts (extend, don't break)\n\n`AgenticStoreContract` composing `NodeStoreContract`:\n- Agents: `putAgent`, `getAgent`, `listAgents`, `updateReputation(agentId, outcome)`\n- Runs: `startRun(spec)`, `appendStep(runId, step)`, `checkpointRun(runId, state)`,\n  `resumeRun(runId)`, `forkRun(runId, goalPatch)`, `enqueueTask(runId, task)`, `drainInbox(runId)`\n- Budgets: `accrueCost(runId, cost)`, `checkBudget(runId, kind)`\n- Tools: `putTool`, `invokeTool(toolId, input)` → `toolCallId`, `putToolset`, `bindToolset`\n- Governance: `putGovernancePolicy`, `evaluateAllocation(policyId, ctx)` → roleBindings\n- Roles: `putRole`, `assignRole(roleId, agentId)`\n- Objectives: `putObjective`, `advanceAgenda(objectiveId)`, `sleepObjective(objectiveId, until)`\n- Beliefs: `putBelief`, `retractBelief`, `getBeliefs(ownerKind, ownerId)`\n- Capabilities: `putCapability`, `bindCapability(capId, runId)`\n- Builder: `startBuilderRun(intent, mode)`, `spawnFromBuilder(builderRunId)`\n\n## 5. Validation / Quickstart (proof the backbone works)\n\nRunnable end-to-end scenarios (contracts exercised, no full impl):\n1. **Human-led spawn**: `startBuilderRun({intent},'human_led')` → `cap-store.agent` → `startRun`\n   (single-role policy, `endStrategy:'graceful'`) → `appendStep(llm_call)` → `checkpointRun` →\n   `resumeRun` (proves durable resume + 3-axis ids).\n2. **Multi-role governance**: policy `round_robin` over 3 agents → `evaluateAllocation` rotates\n   `roleBindings` across 3 `startRun` calls; then `cost_aware` policy picks lowest-`avgCostCents`\n   agent given `costBudgetCents` (proves economic/reputation allocation).\n3. **Tool generation + deferred approval**: `putTool({kind:'generated'})` → `invokeTool` from a\n   `tool_call` step whose `callStatus='pending_human'` → HITL gate resolves → step completes\n   (proves on-the-fly tools + deferred/approval model + causal edge `invoked_in`).\n4. **Agent-led build (recursion)**: an `agent_run` step `actionType='spawn'` → `startBuilderRun(...,'agent_led')`\n   → child `cap-store.agent` + child `agent_run` (proves recursive construction).\n5. **Objective across runs**: `putObjective({agenda:[task,sleep_until,review]})` → run #1 does `task`,\n   `sleepObjective`; run #2 (later) `advanceAgenda` → `review` → `succeeded` (proves cross-run intent).\n6. **Capability as data**: bind a `cap-store.capability{kind:'budget'}` to a run → `checkBudget`\n   raises `BudgetExceededError` (proves behavior-as-Node, no engine change).\n7. **Causal provenance walk**: from a `cap-store.memory` Node, traverse `emits`→`agent_step`→\n   `agent_run`→`governed_by`→`governance_policy`→`defines`→`role`→`played_by`→`agent`→`pursues`→`objective`.\n8. **Time-travel**: `getNodeAtVersion(agentRunId, 1)` vs current → `forkRun`.\n\n## 6. Risks / Open Questions\n\n- **R1 — Query performance**: universal Node + json payloads. 22: // ── Shared: actor reference ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
23: // A human and an agent are interchangeable as edge/author endpoints. This is the

26: export const ActorRefSchema = z.object({
27:   kind: z.enum(['user', 'agent']),
28:   id: z.string().min(1),
29: })
30: export type ActorRef = z.infer<typeof ActorRefSchema>
31: 
32: export function actorDid(a: ActorRef): string {
33:   return `${a.kind}:${a.id}`
34: }
35: 
36: export function parseActorDid(did: string | null | undefined): ActorRef | null {
37:   if (!did) return null
38:   const i = did.indexOf(':')
39:   if (i < 0) return null
40:   const kind = did.slice(0, i)
41:   const id = did.slice(i + 1)
42:   if ((kind === 'user' || kind === 'agent') && id) return { kind, id }
43:   return null
44: }

Backbone Entities (schemas already exist in `src/schema/agentic.ts`)\n\n| Node type | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| `cap-store.agent` | Agent as actor; reputation derived from run outcomes; `createdByActor` |\n| `cap-store.role` | Governance slot; `constraintsJson{maxCostCents,maxTokens,allowBrowser,allowTools,maxSteps}` |\n| `cap-store.governance_policy` | Multi-role allocation; `strategy`, `roles[]`, `endStrategy`, `costBudgetCents`, `reputationFloor` |\n| `cap-store.agent_run` | Durable/resumable/forkable spine; `runId`/`conversationId`/`objectiveId`; `checkpointJson`; `budget` |\n| `cap-store.agent_step` | Atomic work unit; `actor:actorRef`; `callStatus: ok|pending_human|deferred|error`; `emitsNodeIds[]` |\n| `cap-store.tool` | Generated/registered tool; `sandboxJson` (deny-all default); `generatedByActor` |\n| `cap-store.objective` | Cross-run intent; `agenda[]` (task/wait_for_event/human_check/sleep_until/review); `progress` |\n| `cap-store.agent_belief` | Versioned mutable world-model; `ownerKind`; `retracted`; `sourceStepId?` |\n| `cap-store.builder_run` | Agent construction (human_led / agent_led); emits `cap-store.agent` |\n\nEdge vocabulary (`AGENTIC_EDGE`): `spawned`, `uses`, `plays`, `played_by`, `defines`, `governs`,\n`child`, `step`, `invoked_in`, `version_of`, `emits`, `believes`, `pursues`, `subtask`, `built`.\n\n## 3. New Relational Tables (Prisma — ADD only)\n\n- `AgentBuilderRun` — build pipeline state (discover→infer→draft→validate→spawn); writes\n  resulting `cap-store.agent` / `cap-store.agent_run` Nodes.\n- `RunInbox` — mid-run task queue (`{ runId, priority:'asap'|'when_idle', contentJson, status }`).\n- `SlotBinding` — audited UI↔agent/role binding (`{ slotId, componentId, boundAgentId?,\n  boundRoleId?, boundByActor, active, auditJson }`) for hot-swappable UI.\n\n## 4. Work Items (ordered, atomic)\n\n1. **Register schemas** — edit `src/schema/schemas.ts` `registerAllSchemas()` to import\n   `agenticDataSchemas` from `./agentic.js` and loop-register each `cap-store.*` agentic type\n   into `schemaRegistry` (with `indexContent`/`embeddingText` per type, mirroring the\n   `cap-store.memory` block). Verify `schemaRegistry.has('cap-store.agent') === true`.\n\n2. **Contracts** — create `src/storage/contracts/agentic-store.ts` exporting\n   `AgenticStoreContract` (composition note: methods persist via `NodeStoreContract`, which\n   already provides `putNode/getNode/listNodes/putEdge/getOutgoingEdges/updateNode/\n   getNodeAtVersion`). Contract methods:\n   - agents: `putAgent`, `getAgent`, `listAgents`, `updateReputation(agentId, outcome)`\n   - runs: `startRun(spec)`, `appendStep(runId, step)`, `checkpointRun(runId, state)`,\n     `resumeRun(runId)`, `forkRun(runId, goalPatch)`, `enqueueTask(runId, task)`, `drainInbox(runId)`\n   - budgets: `accrueCost(runId, cost)`, `checkBudget(runId, kind)`\n   - tools: `putTool`, `invokeTool(toolId, input) -> toolCallId`, `putToolset`, `bindToolset`\n   - governance: `putGovernancePolicy`, `evaluateAllocation(policyId, ctx) -> roleBindings`\n   - roles: `putRole`, `assignRole(roleId, agentId)`\n   - objectives: `putObjective`, `advanceAgenda(objectiveId)`, `sleepObjective(id, until)`\n   - beliefs: `putBelief`, `retractBelief`, `getBeliefs(ownerKind, ownerId)`\n   - capabilities: `putCapability`, `bindCapability(capId, runId)`\n   - builder: `startBuilderRun(intent, mode)`, `spawnFromBuilder(builderRunId)`\n\n3. **Prisma migration** — add `AgentBuilderRun`, `RunInbox`, `SlotBinding` models to\n   `prisma/schema.prisma`; run `bunx prisma migrate dev`; add an `--accept-data-loss` fixture\n   push for the test DB (`DATABASE_URL=\"file:./tests/fixtures/node-store-test.db\" bunx prisma db push`).\n\n4. **GovernanceEngine** — `evaluateAllocation(policyId, ctx)`: round_robin cursor +\n   `cost_aware` (pick min `avgCostCents` among candidates within `costBudgetCents`) +\n   `reputationFloor` filter + `fallback_chain`; honor `endStrategy`\n   (early/graceful/exhaustive) when resolving parallel tool calls / final output.\n\n5. **BudgetEngine** — `accrueCost` + `checkBudget` vs `UsageLimits`\n   (`requestLimit`, `toolCallsLimit`, `inputTokensLimit`, `outputTokensLimit`,\n   `totalTokensLimit`); raise new `BudgetExceededError` (extend `src/errors.ts` error hierarchy).\n\n6. **ToolRegistry + SandboxRunner wiring** — `putTool({kind:'generated'})` defaults to deny-all\n   sandbox; `invokeTool` returns a `toolCallId`; toolsets are `cap-store.tool`-binding Nodes.\n\n7. **ObjectiveEngine** — agenda advance, `sleepObjective`/`wake`, cross-run pursuit; produces\n   `cap-store.objective` Nodes + `pursues` edges.\n\n8. **BeliefStore** — `putBelief`/`retractBelief`/`getBeliefs`; each mutation bumps Node version\n   (time-travelable via `updateNode`/`getNodeAtVersion`).\n\n9. **CapabilityBinder** — bind `cap-store.capability` Nodes to runs; toposort by `ordering`\n   (`wraps`/`wrappedBy`/`requires`).\n\n10. **AgentBuilder subsystem** — `AgentBuilderRun` service: `startBuilderRun` + `spawnFromBuilder`\n    (human-led emits agent; agent-led triggered by `agent_step.actionType='spawn'`).\n\n11. **SlotBinding** — UI hot-swap audit hook writing `SlotBinding` rows.\n\n12. **Back-compat** — one-way sync view `AgentLoopRun` → `cap-store.agent_run` (read-only post-transition).\n\n13. **Quickstart integration tests** — `tests/integration/agentic/` covering the 8 scenarios in §6.\n\n## 5. Cross-Cutting Rules (invariants)\n\n- **Actor uniformity**: `actorRef={kind:'user'|'agent',id}`; `authorDid = kind:id`.\n- **Three identity axes** never overloaded: `runId` (one execution) ⊥ `conversationId`\n  (one thread) ⊥ `objectiveId` (one pursuit across runs).\n- **Cost is first-class**; `BudgetExceededError` raised before/after calls.\n- **Durable by default**: `checkpointJson`, `RunInbox`, `capability.configJson` are serializable\n  (no runtime closures) — satisfies pydantic-ai `durable_exec` rule so runs resume across restarts.\n- **Add, never rewrite** the ~150 existing models. `AgentLoopRun`/`AgentStep` stay read-only.\n- Generated `cap-store.tool` defaults to deny-all; `SandboxRunner` enforces.\n\n## 6. Validation (quickstart scenarios → integration tests)\n\n1. Multi-role governance: `round_robin` rotates `roleBindings` across 3 `startRun` calls; then\n   `cost_aware` picks lowest-`avgCostCents` within `costBudgetCents`.\n3. Tool generation + deferred approval: `putTool({kind:'generated'})` → `invokeTool` step with\n   `callStatus='pending_human'` → HITL resolves → step completes (causal `invoked_in` edge).\n4. Agent-led recursion: `agent_run` step `actionType='spawn'` → `startBuilderRun(...,'agent_led')`\n   → child `cap-store.agent` + child `agent_run`.\n5. ## Assistant (Ask · Tencent: Hy3 (free) · 12.7s)

Short answer: **yes, the message/action/conversation data model is already fully accounted for** outside the agentic backbone — and I designed the backbone to *reference* it rather than duplicate it. No new message/action model is needed inside the plan.

Here's exactly how the two layers relate:

| Concern | Where it lives (already exists) | What the agentic backbone adds |
|---|---|---|
| Chat messages, threads, attachments | `Conversation`, `ConversationMessage`, `MessageAttachment` (Prisma) + `cap-store.message`/`cap-store.conversation` Nodes | `agent_run.conversationId` links a run to an existing thread — **3rd identity axis** |
| Agent's own step-by-step actions | `AgentStep`, `AgentLoopRun` (legacy), and new `cap-store.agent_step` Node | `agent_step` is the *causal* unit (which agent, which role, what tool call, which nodes it emitted). This is the missing link the legacy `AgentStep` didn't have. |
| Tool calls / actions invoked | `Tool`/`ToolCall` concepts + new `cap-store.tool` Node | `agent_step.toolCallId` + `invoked_in` edge ties a step to the exact tool call |
| Tool definitions | (none generic today) | `cap-store.tool` — generated/on-the-fly tools (deny-all sandbox default) |
| Workflows / DAG actions | `WorkflowDefinition`/`WorkflowNode`/`WorkflowEdge` | A workflow node can reference a `cap-store.agent_run`/`cap-store.tool` by id (composition, not reimplementation) |

So the design deliberately **does not** re-create message/action models. Two reasons, both in the plan's constraints:

1. **"Add, never rewrite the ~150 existing models"** — `ConversationMessage` + `AgentStep` already exist; I keep them and add the *missing* causal/provenance layer (`cap-store.agent_step` with `emitsNodeIds` + `invoked_in`/`emits` edges) on top.
2. **Unify onto the Node graph** — messages and conversations already have `cap-store.message` / `cap-store.conversation` Node representations (used by `ConversationManager.captureAsNode()`), so the agentic run just points at them via `conversationId` and `emits`.

The one gap worth calling out: the **agent's chat-style message history as an *actor***. Your earlier decision was "agents are users with profiles/history." That's modeled via:
- the `actor` field on every `agent_step` (`ActorRef{kind:'agent', id}`) — so an agent's action history is queryable as `all agent_step where actor = agent:X`,
- `cap-store.agent.createdByActor` + reputation derived from run outcomes,
- and agents can author Nodes (`authorDid = "agent:<id>"`), so an agent's "messages" are just Nodes it emitted (same as a user's).

If you want a *first-class agent chat thread* (an agent talking to a user in a dedicated conversation, distinct from runs), that would be a small addition — but it'd reuse `Conversation`/`ConversationMessage`, not a new model. 

Do you want me to (a) keep it as-is (reference existing message/action models), or (b) add an explicit "agent conversation thread" surface? For the plan as written, (a) is correct and I'll continue implementing the backbone.

yes we need to add that to our plan and design - here is some additonal context Skip `opencode run` as your integration point entirely — it's just a CLI wrapper around the same HTTP server, and there's a known bug where `run --attach` throws "No context found for instance" on exactly the pattern you'd want (attaching to a long-running `serve` instance). Don't fight that.

**Talk to `opencode serve` directly as an HTTP/SSE backend, not as a subprocess-per-call.**

Fits your fleet-supervisor pattern almost exactly:

- `opencode serve --port 4096 --hostname 127.0.0.1` — spawn it once, supervise it the way you supervise Chrome instances (HealthProbe against `GET /global/health`, restart-with-backoff on crash, not per-request spawn/kill).
- `POST /session` to create a session, `POST /session/:id/message` to send a prompt and block for the reply, or `POST /session/:id/prompt_async` (204, fire-and-forget) if you're streaming results back through your own delta-sync layer instead.
- `GET /event` — SSE stream of the entire bus (session updates, tool calls, permission requests). This is your ingestion point into whatever you're doing for real-time deltas in cap-store — treat it like another WebSocket source feeding the same pipeline that (once you fix the `ws.onmessage` bug) feeds your frontend.
- `POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID` — this is the piece that actually solves the non-interactive automation problem people are hitting on GitHub. Don't rely on `--auto` or agent permission presets to get you fully headless; those are inconsistently enforced at session bootstrap in the version people are complaining about. Instead, listen on `/event` for permission-request events and respond programmatically — you own the policy decision in your own code, which is more in line with your Governor Canon instinct anyway (one authority decides, not a CLI flag buried in agent frontmatter).
- Custom agent via `opencode agent create --permissions bash,read,edit,glob,grep,webfetch` (non-interactive, all four flags passed) gives you the baseline tool grants; the permission-response loop above handles anything not pre-granted.

**Auth**: set `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`, basic auth, keep it bound to loopback — no reason to expose it beyond localhost given your local-first posture.

**Client**: generate off `GET /doc` (OpenAPI 3.1) rather than pulling in their JS SDK wholesale — smaller footprint, matches your no-off-the-shelf-framework bias, and you already have the Prisma/Bun typing discipline to hand-roll a thin typed fetch wrapper.

One open question worth deciding now: do you want OpenCode as a peer provider alongside your Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini CDP-driven sessions in the same ProviderAdapter trait, or as a separate execution tier entirely (since it's a real API-driven agent, not a browser session you're puppeteering)? That changes whether the `/event` SSE feed goes into the same event substrate as your browser fleet or gets its own lane. Two decisions before schema, because getting these wrong means rebuilding later:

**1. Don't give OpenCode its own database file that VIVIM writes to.** OpenCode already has its own SQLite (`opencode db path`). Let it own that — single-writer discipline means you never want two processes fighting over the same file. VIVIM's Prisma/SQLite store becomes a **mirror + audit layer**, populated asynchronously by consuming the `/event` SSE stream. OpenCode's DB is ephemeral working state; yours is the durable record.

**2. Don't build a new event log for this.** You already designed a hash-chained event substrate with a durable outbox for the capability layer. OpenCode becomes just another event producer into that same substrate, tagged by source. If you give it a parallel logging system you've recreated the exact dual-tracking problem you flagged for Prisma-vs-VersionManager, one level down.

Schema, built on those two calls:

```prisma
model AgentSession {
  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  providerSessionId String   @unique          // opencode's session id
  providerId        String   @default("opencode")
  parentSessionId   String?                    // fork lineage
  parent            AgentSession? @relation("Fork", fields: [parentSessionId], references: [id])
  forks             AgentSession[] @relation("Fork")
  agentName         String                     // which opencode agent/permission preset
  model             String                     // provider/model
  projectPath       String
  status            String   @default("active") // active|aborted|archived
  createdAt         DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt         DateTime @updatedAt

  messages     AgentMessage[]
  permissions  AgentPermissionDecision[]
  fileEdits    AgentFileEdit[]
}

model AgentMessage {
  id                 String   @id @default(cuid())
  agentSessionId     String
  session            AgentSession @relation(fields: [agentSessionId], references: [id])
  providerMessageId  String   @unique
  role               String                   // user|assistant
  sequence           Int                       // ordering within session
  createdAt          DateTime @default(now())

  parts AgentMessagePart[]

  @@index([agentSessionId, sequence])
}

model AgentMessagePart {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  messageId    String
  message      AgentMessage @relation(fields: [messageId], references: [id])
  partIndex    Int
  type         String        // text|tool_call|tool_result|file|reasoning
  toolName     String?
  toolCallId   String?
  status       String?       // pending|running|completed|error
  content      String        // JSON blob, keep raw shape from opencode
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([messageId, partIndex])
}

// This is the important one — treat every permission prompt as a
// governance event, not just UI state. This is your audit trail for
// "what did the agent get to do without a human."
model AgentPermissionDecision {
  id                String   @id @default(cuid())
  agentSessionId    String
  session           AgentSession @relation(fields: [agentSessionId], references: [id])
  providerPermissionId String
  toolName          String
  riskTier          Int           // reuse your existing capability risk-tier scale
  requestedAt       DateTime
  respondedAt       DateTime?
  decision          String?       // allow|deny|allow_always
  decidedBy         String        // "policy:auto-approve-tier1" | "human:<userId>"
  payload           String        // raw JSON of the request

  @@index([agentSessionId])
}

// File-level truth, derived from /session/:id/diff — this is what actually
// touched your filesystem, independent of chat noise
model AgentFileEdit {
  id             String   @id @default(cuid())
  agentSessionId String
  session        AgentSession @relation(fields: [agentSessionId], references: [id])
  messageId      String?
  filePath       String
  patch          String        // store as your existing versioned JSON Patch format, not raw unified diff — one patch format across the whole system
  beforeHash     String?
  afterHash      String?
  createdAt      DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([filePath])
}

// Mirrors opencode's own agent frontmatter — lets you version-control
// agent/permission presets as data instead of only as files on disk
model AgentDefinition {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  name         String   @unique
  mode         String                // all|primary|subagent
  permissions  String                // JSON array
  model        String
  systemPrompt String?
  version      Int      @default(1)
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
}
```

The `AgentEvent` outbox itself I'd deliberately leave out of this list — don't create it here, extend your existing hash-chained event table with `source: "opencode"` and `providerSessionId` as a correlation key. Every row above should be derivable by replaying that outbox; these tables are read-model projections, not sources of truth. That's the same pattern you already committed to for the browser fleet, and it's the only way OpenCode and your CDP-driven providers end up queryable through one lens instead of two.

Where does `AgentDefinition.version` sit relative to your still-unresolved Prisma-vs-VersionManager question? That's the one place this schema forces the issue — happy to help you actually settle that if you want to use this as the forcing function.  ////// assess what to keep from that
