No schema duplication; one query lens for human + agent + provider threads.\n\n## 6c. OpenCode Integration — HTTP/SSE Backend (NEW — added to plan)\n\n**Decisions locked (2026-07-19):**\n- **Skip `opencode run`** entirely (CLI wrapper + known `run --attach` \"No context found\"\n  bug). Talk to **`opencode serve`** as a long-lived HTTP/SSE backend, supervised like a\n  Chrome slave (HealthProbe `GET /global/health`, restart-with-backoff).\n- **Peer provider** (user-confirmed): OpenCode = `providerId='opencode'` reusing\n  `ProviderSession`/`Conversation`/`ConversationMessage`/`StreamBlock`. NO parallel\n  `AgentMessage`/`AgentMessagePart` tables (they'd duplicate `ConversationMessage`/`StreamBlock`).\n- **Mirror + audit, never write OpenCode's DB**: VIVIM store is populated asynchronously by\n  consuming `GET /event` SSE. OpenCode's SQLite stays single-writer/ephemeral.\n- **Governor owns permission decisions**: listen on `/event` for permission-request events,\n  respond via `POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID` programmatically (not `--auto` /\n  agent frontmatter presets). Matches Governor Canon (one authority decides).\n- `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` basic auth, loopback-bound. Thin typed fetch client generated off\n  `GET /doc` (OpenAPI 3.1) — no off-the-shelf JS SDK.\n\n### Reconciliation note (deviations from the pasted schema — verified against actual code)\n1. **No `AgentMessage`/`AgentMessagePart`** — dropped; reuse `ConversationMessage`+`StreamBlock`.\n2. **No existing durable event substrate** — the pasted \"hash-chained outbox\" does NOT exist;\n   `CapabilityEventBus` is in-memory/transient and there is no `Event`/`Outbox` table. To honor\n   the *intent* (single source of truth, no dual-tracking) we add **one minimal durable\n   `EventRecord` outbox** (source-tagged) that OpenCode + browser fleet + capability layer all\n   write to. This is the only new \"event log\"; it is the shared substrate, not a parallel one.\n3. **No `riskTier` capability column** — capabilities use `planTier`; the real sensitivity scale\n   is `securityLevel` (Int) on Node. OpenCode `AgentPermissionDecision.riskTier` becomes a local\n   `Int` (1-5) mapped onto `securityLevel` semantics; document the mapping.\n4. **No canonical JSON Patch helper** — `AgentFileEdit.patch` stored as RFC-6902 JSON Patch\n   (new, simple convention); `beforeHash`/`afterHash` from file content.\n5. **`Prisma-vs-VersionManager`** question: OpenCode tables are **read-model projections** derived\n   by replaying `EventRecord`; `AgentDefinition.version` is a plain `Int` (bump on edit), NOT the\n   Node version chain. Settled as: these tables are projections, `EventRecord` is source of truth.\n\n### New Prisma tables (ADD only)\n- `EventRecord` — durable outbox: `{ id, source(String), entityType?, entityId?, providerSessionId?, type(String), payloadJson, seq(Int), hash(String), createdAt }`. `source` ∈\n  `{'opencode','browser_fleet','capability', ...}`. Hash-chained (`hash` = H(prevHash||payload)).\n- `AgentSession` — OpenCode supervision extension of `ProviderSession`: `{ id PK, providerSessionId @unique (opencode's), providerId @default(\"opencode\"), parentSessionId? (fork), agentName, model, projectPath, status, createdAt, updatedAt }`; relation `ProviderSession` (1:1 optional) + self `Fork`.\n- `AgentPermissionDecision` — governance audit: `{ id, agentSessionId, providerPermissionId @unique, toolName, riskTier(Int), requestedAt, respondedAt?, decision? ('allow'|'deny'|'allow_always'), decidedBy, payloadJson }`.\n- `AgentFileEdit` — filesystem truth from `/session/:id/diff`: `{ id, agentSessionId, messageId?, filePath, patchJson (RFC-6902), beforeHash?, afterHash?, createdAt }`.\n- `AgentDefinition` — versioned agent/permission presets as data: `{ id, name @unique, mode ('all'|'primary'|'subagent'), permissionsJson, model, systemPrompt?, version @default(1), createdAt }`.\n\n### New engine / client\n- `src/engines/opencode-client.ts` — typed fetch wrapper (sessions, message, prompt_async,\n  permissions, `/event` SSE consumer, `/doc` parse). HealthProbe + backoff supervisor.\n- `src/engines/opencode-ingest.ts` — SSE → `EventRecord` → project into `ConversationMessage`/\n  `StreamBlock`/`AgentPermissionDecision`/`AgentFileEdit`; Governor permission-response loop.\n- Extend `EventRecord` writer into `CapabilityEventBus` (emit to both in-memory bus + durable table).\n\n### Validation scenarios (add to §6)\n9. OpenCode peer session: spawn `opencode serve`, `POST /session`, `POST /session/:id/message`,\n   assert a `ConversationMessage` (role=assistant, `blocksJson` with tool_call) is projected.\n10. Permission governance: emit a permission-request on `/event` → Governor auto-denies tier>3\n    → `POST /session/:id/permissions/:id` → `AgentPermissionDecision` row written by policy.\n11. File edit truth: `/session/:id/diff` → `AgentFileEdit` patch stored; replayable from `EventRecord`.\n\n## 7. Risks / Open Questions"

1: // src/engines/event-record-store.ts
2: // EventRecordStore — durable, hash-chained outbox (shared event substrate).
3: //
4: // OpenCode + browser fleet + capability layer all write here. The hash chain is
5: // H(prevHash || payload) per source; seq is monotonic per source. This is the
6: // single source of truth; projections (ConversationMessage, AgentPermissionDecision,
7: // AgentFileEdit) are replayed FROM these records, never dual-tracked.
8: 
9: import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
10: import type { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client'
11: import { newId } from '../ids.js'
12: 
13: export type EventSource = 'opencode' | 'browser_fleet' | 'capability' | string
14: 
15: export interface EventRecordInput {
16:   source: EventSource
17:   type: string
18:   entityType?: string
19:   entityId?: string
20:   providerSessionId?: string
21:   payload: unknown
22: }
23: 
24: export interface EventRecordRow {
25:   id: string
26:   source: string
27:   entityType: string | null
28:   entityId: string | null
29:   providerSessionId: string | null
30:   type: string
31:   payloadJson: string
32:   seq: number
33:   hash: string
34:   createdAt: number
35: }
36: 
37: export class EventRecordStore {
38:   constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaClient) {}
39: 
40:   private chainHash(prevHash: string, payloadJson: string): string {
41:     return createHash('sha256').update(`${prevHash}||${payloadJson}`).digest('hex')
42:   }
43: 
44:   private async lastHashAndSeq(source: string): Promise<{ hash: string; seq: number }> {
45:     const rows = await this.prisma.eventRecord.findMany({
46:       where: { source },
47:       orderBy: { seq: 'desc' },
48:       take: 1,
49:     })
50:     const last = rows[0] as EventRecordRow | undefined
51:     return { hash: last?.hash ?? 'GENESIS', seq: last?.seq ?? 0 }
52:   }
53: 
54:   /** Append an event, extending the per-source hash chain. Idempotent on entityId. */
55:   async append(input: EventRecordInput): Promise<EventRecordRow> {
56:     const { source, type, entityType, entityId, providerSessionId, payload } = input
57:     if (entityId && providerSessionId) {
58:       const existing = await this.prisma.eventRecord.findFirst({
59:         where: { source, entityType, entityId },
60:       })
61:       if (existing) return existing as unknown as EventRecordRow
62:     }
63:     const { hash: prevHash, seq } = await this.lastHashAndSeq(source)
64:     const payloadJson = JSON.stringify(payload ?? {})
65:     const hash = this.chainHash(prevHash, payloadJson)
66:     const row = await this.prisma.eventRecord.create({
67:       data: {
68:         id: newId(),
69:         source,
70:         entityType: entityType ?? null,
71:         entityId: entityId ?? null,
72:         providerSessionId: providerSessionId ?? null,
73:         type,
74:         payloadJson,
75:         seq: seq + 1,
76:         hash,
77:         createdAt: Date.now(),
78:       },
79:     })
80:     return row as unknown as EventRecordRow
81:   }
82: 
83:   async list(source?: string, limit = 100): Promise<EventRecordRow[]> {
84:     const rows = await this.prisma.eventRecord.findMany({
85:       where: source ? { source } : {},
86:       orderBy: { seq: 'asc' },
87:       take: limit,
88:     })
89:     return rows as unknown as EventRecordRow[]
90:   }
91: 
92:   /** Verify the chain integrity for a source (returns first break, or null). */
93:   async verifyChain(source: string): Promise<{ ok: boolean; brokenAtSeq?: number }> {
94:     const rows = (await this.prisma.eventRecord.findMany({
95:       where: { source },
96:       orderBy: { seq: 'asc' },
97:     })) as unknown as EventRecordRow[]
98:     let prevHash = 'GENESIS'
99:     for (const r of rows) {
100:       const expected = this.chainHash(prevHash, r.payloadJson)
101:       if (expected !== r.hash) return { ok: false, brokenAtSeq: r.seq }
102:       prevHash = r.hash
103:     }
104:     return { ok: true }
105:   }
106: }

  async startAgentConversation(
    actor: ActorRef,
    goal: string,
    opts?: { title?: string; agentId?: string },
  ): Promise<{ providerSessionId: string; conversationId: string }> {
    const agentId = opts?.agentId ?? actor.id
    const providerSessionId = await this.ensureAgentProviderSession(agentId)
    const conversationId = newId()
    const ts = now()
    await this.prisma.conversation.create({
      data: {
        id: conversationId,
        providerSessionId,
        providerId: `agent:${agentId}`,
        title: opts?.title ?? goal.slice(0, 80),
        state: 'active',
        messageCount: 0,
        contextJson: JSON.stringify({ goal, actorDid: actorDid(actor) }),
        createdAt: ts,
        updatedAt: ts,
      },
    })
    // Author the opening goal as a user message (one query lens for all threads).
    await this.appendAgentMessage(conversationId, {
      role: 'user',
      text: goal,
      authorDid: actorDid(actor),
    })
    return { providerSessionId, conversationId }
  }

  async appendAgentMessage(

        id,

        sequenceIndex: count,
        model: msg.model ?? null,
        metadataJson: JSON.stringify({ authorDid: msg.authorDid ?? null, stepId: msg.stepId ?? null }),
        createdAt: ts,
        updatedAt: ts,
      },
    })
    await this.prisma.conversation.update({
      where: { id: conversationId },
      data: { messageCount: { increment: 1 }, lastMessageAt: ts, updatedAt: ts },
    })
    let idx = 0
    for (const b of blocks) {
      await this.prisma.streamBlock.create({
        data: {
          id: newId(),
          conversationId,
          messageId: id,
          blockIndex: idx++,
          blockKind: b.kind,
          blockData: JSON.stringify(b.data),
          blockMeta: JSON.stringify(b.meta ?? {}),
          createdAt: ts,
        },
      })
    }
    // Causal link: the producing step emits this message node.
    if (msg.stepId) await this.linkStepToMessage(msg.stepId, id)
    return { id }
  }

6. **Permission model & tool gating** — `permission: allow|ask|deny` + glob, `permission.task`; how `ask` resolves headlessly under `--auto`; deny-by-default behavior + exit semantics.
7. **Multi-turn / session resume & forking** — `-s/--session`, `-c/--continue`, `--fork`; on-disk session artifact; verify `--continue` vs prompt+`--auto` exclusivity claim; `export`/`import`/`session list|delete`.

10. **Config precedence, providers & model routing** — resolution order (global → project `opencode.json` → `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`); `model`/`small_model`/per-agent override; `{env:VAR}` trust boundary (global only); how the `opencode/` Zen group registers. # Feature Specification: Local-Agent OpenCode Provider (Zen free models)

**Feature Branch**: `022-local-agent-opencode`

**Created**: 2026-07-19

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Wire the 4 verified Zen free OpenCode models (deepseek-v4-flash-free, hy3-free, mimo-v2.5-free, north-mini-code-free) into vivim as a `local-agent` provider so the UnifiedCapabilityRegistry can dispatch them without CDP/Chrome."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Register local-agent provider + capabilities (Priority: P1)

vivim boots, seeds a `local-agent` provider manifest (`slug: opencode`) with 4 Zen free
models, and registers a `cap:agent:run` UnifiedCapability so any surface (CLI/UI/API/MCP)
can dispatch an OpenCode agent task. No browser, no CDP, no ChromeGovernor.

**Why this priority**: This is the minimal shippable integration — it makes the 4 verified
free models first-class vivim capabilities without touching the Governor Canon.

**Independent Test**: `bun run devops runtime-test status --provider=opencode` shows the
provider seeded with 4 models; `bun run devops runtime-test test --nl "run deepseek agent: say hello"`
returns a parsed `ContentBlock[]` text.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a fresh boot, **When** `registerDefaultCapabilities` + local-agent seed runs, **Then** a provider row `opencode` with `provider_type='local-agent'` and 4 model rows exists.
2. **Given** the registry, **When** `cap:agent:run` is executed with `model: 'opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free'`, **Then** an `opencode run --auto --format json` subprocess is spawned and its stdout parsed to `ContentBlock[]`.
3. **Given** `nemotron-3-ultra-free` is requested, **When** dispatched, **Then** it is rejected with `EngineError` (model not in allowed list).

---

### User Story 2 - LocalAgentProviderExecutor parses `--format json` (Priority: P2)

  The executor wraps `opencode run` and converts the **verified** opencode v1.17.15 NDJSON event
  stream into the canonical `ContentBlock[]` consumed by `StreamParserEngine` /
  `ConversationManager.captureAsNode()`.

  **Verified parse contract** (see `docs/research/briefs/opencode-deep/area-01-cli-run.md`,
  `area-02-tooluse.md`, `area-06-permissions.md`, `area-08-streaming.md`):
  - `--format json` emits **NDJSON** — one JSON object per line (NO array, NO envelope).
  - Each line has a top-level `type`; assistant content lives in `part.text` / `part.type`
    (NOT the legacy `message.parts` / `role` shape).
  - Event types: `step_start`, `text`, `reasoning` (only with `--thinking`), `tool_use`,
    `step_finish`, `error`.
  - `tool_use` → `tool-call` + `tool-result` blocks. `part.tool === 'invalid'` is a **silent
    permission denial** (run still exits 0) → `PERMISSION_DENIED` error block + `capability:failed`.
  - `sessionID` is captured from the first `step_start` and returned for multi-turn resume.

  **Why this priority**: The parse contract is what lets downstream engines treat agent
  output identically to provider output — no special-casing elsewhere.

  **Independent Test**: `tests/unit/engines/local-agent.test.ts` feeds a recorded `--format json`
  payload through `parseOpencodeJson()` and asserts text/tool/permission-denial/reasoning blocks
  and `cost:0` (8/8 passing).

  **Acceptance Scenarios**:

  1. **Given** a `--format json` stdout with a `text` event, **When** parsed, **Then** a `ContentBlock` of type `text` is produced.

# Implementation Plan: Local-Agent OpenCode Provider (Zen free models)

**Branch**: `022-local-agent-opencode` | **Date**: 2026-07-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `specs/022-local-agent-opencode/spec.md`

## Summary

Wire the 4 verified Zen free OpenCode models as a `local-agent` provider so the
`UnifiedCapabilityRegistry` can dispatch them via a `cap:agent:run` capability. The executor
shells `opencode run --auto --model <allowed> --format json` and parses stdout into the
canonical `ContentBlock[]` — no CDP, no ChromeGovernor (Governor Canon preserved).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.x (strict, ESNext) / Bun runtime
**Primary Dependencies**: Bun, Prisma v6.5, Zod, React 18
**Storage**: SQLite via Prisma (dev.db) — provider + model + capability rows
**Testing**: Bun test runner (`bun test`)
**Target Platform**: Windows (PowerShell 7+), Bun HTTP server
**Project Type**: Full-stack monorepo (13 engines + API + React frontend)
**Linter/Formatter**: Biome
**Build**: tsup (ESM + DTS)

**Performance Goals**: Agent cold-start latency observed 37–54s on this host; hard `timeoutMs` 120s.
**Constraints**: Governor Canon (no engine imports BunCdpClient); Store Contracts (engines depend on contracts, not impls); One Entry Point (every op is a UnifiedCapability); Custom errors (no raw `new Error()` in engines); TypeScript strict (no `any`, `type` imports, `.js` extensions).

**Verified ground truth (2026-07-19, executed on host)**:
- `opencode` on PATH; Zen free models cost 0, no key.
- Working: `opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free` (~43s), `opencode/hy3-free` (~54s),
  `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` (~41s), `opencode/north-mini-code-free` (~37s).
- Broken: `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (no output in 5 min) — excluded.
- `--format json` stream: `{type:'step_start'|'text'|'step_finish', part:{type:'text',text}, tokens:{cost:0}}`.
- `serve` starts unsecured unless `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` set — out of scope for v1.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before implementation. Re-check after design.*

- [x] Governor Canon: `LocalAgentProviderExecutor` shells `opencode` via `Bun.spawn`; imports nothing from `chrome-governor` or `BunCdpClient`.

=== setup-plan.ps1 ===
#!/usr/bin/env pwsh
# Setup implementation plan for a feature

[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [switch]$Json,
    [switch]$Help
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'

# Show help if requested
if ($Help) {
    Write-Output "Usage: ./setup-plan.ps1 [-Json] [-Help]"
    Write-Output "  -Json     Output results in JSON format"
    Write-Output "  -Help     Show this help message"
    exit 0
}

# Load common functions
. "$PSScriptRoot/common.ps1"

# Get all paths and variables from common functions
$paths = Get-FeaturePathsEnv

# Ensure the feature directory exists
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $paths.FEATURE_DIR -Force | Out-Null

# Copy plan template if plan doesn't already exist
if (Test-Path $paths.IMPL_PLAN -PathType Leaf) {
    if ($Json) {
        [Console]::Error.WriteLine("Plan already exists at $($paths.IMPL_PLAN), skipping template copy")
    } else {
        Write-Output "Plan already exists at $($paths.IMPL_PLAN), skipping template copy"
    }
} else {
    $template = Resolve-Template -TemplateName 'plan-template' -RepoRoot $paths.REPO_ROOT
    if ($template -and (Test-Path $template)) {
        # Read the template content and write it to the implementation plan file with UTF-8 encoding without BOM
        $content = [System.IO.File]::ReadAllText($template)
        $utf8NoBom = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)
        [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText($paths.IMPL_PLAN, $content, $utf8NoBom)
        # Emit the copy status like the bash twin (setup-plan.sh); route to stderr
        # in -Json mode so stdout stays pure JSON, matching the sibling messages.
        if ($Json) {
            [Console]::Error.WriteLine("Copied plan template to $($paths.IMPL_PLAN)")
        } else {
            Write-Output "Copied plan template to $($paths.IMPL_PLAN)"
        }
    } else {
        # Match the bash twin's wording and stream routing (stderr in -Json so
        # stdout stays pure JSON, stdout otherwise), consistent with the sibling
        # "Copied plan template" message above.
        if ($Json) {
            [Console]::Error.WriteLine("Warning: Plan template not found")
        } else {
            Write-Output "Warning: Plan template not found"
        }
        # Create a basic plan file if template doesn't exist
        New-Item -ItemType File -Path $paths.IMPL_PLAN -Force | Out-Null
    }
}

# Output results
if ($Json) {
    $result = [PSCustomObject]@{
        FEATURE_SPEC = $paths.FEATURE_SPEC
        IMPL_PLAN = $paths.IMPL_PLAN
        SPECS_DIR = $paths.FEATURE_DIR
        BRANCH = $paths.CURRENT_BRANCH
    }
    $result | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
} else {
    Write-Output "FEATURE_SPEC: $($paths.FEATURE_SPEC)"
    Write-Output "IMPL_PLAN: $($paths.IMPL_PLAN)"
    Write-Output "SPECS_DIR: $($paths.FEATURE_DIR)"
    Write-Output "BRANCH: $($paths.CURRENT_BRANCH)"
}

=== constitution ===
# VIVIM Constitution

## Core Principles

### I. Governor Canon (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
Only `ChromeGovernor` touches CDP (`BunCdpClient`). No engine imports `BunCdpClient` directly.
This is enforced by `bun run devops invariants check --category B` and is a hard gate.
Exempt entities must be documented in invariants.ts.

### II. Store Contracts (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
Engines depend on `src/storage/contracts/*.ts` interfaces, never `src/storage/impl/*.ts`.
Implementation details are hidden behind contracts. This enables testing with mock stores
and prevents coupling to Prisma or storage internals.

### III. One Entry Point (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
Every operation is a `UnifiedCapability`. CLI and frontend are thin NL shells that
call `POST /api/interpret` → `POST /api/capabilities/:id/execute`.
- New capability: register in `registerDefaultCapabilities` / a `*caps.ts` module.
- New NL phrase: add a pattern to `catalog.ts` bound to a `capabilityId`.
- Never: hand-write CLI commands, hand-write UI actions, or open a second transport.

### IV. Research-First
No implementation without research report classification. Phase N requires Phase N-1 complete.
Evidence-before-action. Truth scans before roadmap modifications.

### V. Code Quality Standards
- TypeScript strict mode, ESNext target, `.js` extension in imports (Bun ESM)
- Prefer `type` imports: `import type { Foo } from './bar.js'`
- No `any` — use `unknown` + type narrowing
- Zod for runtime validation at boundaries
- Custom error classes from `src/errors.ts` — never raw `new Error()`
- ULID for IDs via `src/ids.ts`
- Barrell exports from `src/index.ts`
- `Result<T, E>` pattern where appropriate

### VI. Testing Gates (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- `bun test` must pass before every commit
- `bun run typecheck` — 0 errors
- `bun run lint` — 0 warnings
- `bun run devops invariants check --category B` — 0 block violations

{
  "content": "# Feature Specification: OpenCode `serve` Backend Integration (v2 persistent harness)\n\n**Feature Branch**: `027-opencode-serve`\n\n**Created**: 2026-07-19\n\n**Status**: Draft\n\n**Input**: User description: \"Connect vivim to a running `opencode serve` process — supervisor, client, and ingest — so OpenCode sessions, permissions, and file edits land in the local DB as a peer provider (`providerId='opencode'`), supervised and governed by the Governor, on top of the agentic backbone AGENT5 already built.\"\n\n## Background & Scope Boundary\n\n- Feature `022-local-agent-opencode` delivered the **v1 one-shot** surface (`cap:agent:run` → `opencode run --auto --format json`). This feature delivers the **v2 persistent** surface: a long-lived `opencode serve` HTTP/SSE backend, supervised locally.\n- The two surfaces are **disjoint transports** over the same `opencode` provider. No shared code paths; both reuse the verified `parseOpencodeJson` event grammar and the `opencode`/`ProviderDefinition` already seeded in `022`.\n- This feature is **additive** and **OFF by default** (local-first principle). It never blocks boot and never requires OpenCode to be up for other providers.\n\n## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*\n\n### User Story 1 - Supervise a local `opencode serve` process (Priority: P1)\n\nvivim can, when explicitly enabled (env flag / capability), spawn and supervise an `opencode serve --port <p> --hostname 127.0.0.1` subprocess with `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` set. It waits for readiness (poll `GET /doc` until 200), restarts on crash with bounded exponential backoff, and shuts the process down cleanly on `SIGTERM`.\n\n**Why this priority**: Without a supervisor there is no durable, observable OpenCode backend — this is the process substrate the client and ingest depend on.\n\n**Independent Test**: `tests/integration/opencode/supervisor.test.ts` (S3) boots `opencode serve`, asserts readiness probe returns 200, asserts `/doc` exposes the session API, then stops the process and asserts exit.\n\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\n\n1. **Given** `OPENCODE_SERVE_ENABLED=1` and a free port, **When** the supervisor starts, **Then** `opencode serve` is spawned on `127.0.0.1` only (never `0.0.0.0`/`--mdns`), with a server password.\n2. **Given** a spawned server, **When** readiness polling runs, **Then** the supervisor proceeds only after `GET /doc` returns 200 (readiness race handled).\n3. **Given** the server crashes, **When** the supervisor detects exit, **Then** it restarts with bounded backoff (max N attempts then gives up, logging).\n4. **Given** a running supervisor, **When** `SIGTERM` arrives, **Then** it kills the child and resolves without orphaning.\n\n### User Story 2 - Client talks the `serve` HTTP/SSE API (Priority: P1)\n\nvivim's client creates a session (`POST /session`), sends a prompt (`POST /session/:id/prompt_async` or `POST /session/:id/message`), and subscribes to the live event stream (`GET /event` SSE). Events are mapped to the canonical `ContentBlock[]` via the **already-verified** `parseOpencodeJson` grammar (same `type`/`part` shape as `--format json`).\n\n**Why this priority**: The client is the bridge that turns a served OpenCode session into vivim-ingestible events.\n\n**Independent Test**: `tests/integration/opencode/client.test.ts` (S1a) against a mock HTTP server implementing the documented endpoints asserts: session created, prompt accepted, SSE frames parsed into `ContentBlock[]` text/tool/permission-denial blocks.\n\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\n\n1. **Given** a live served OpenCode, **When** `client.createSession()` runs, **Then** it returns a `sessionId` and the supervisor registers an `AgentSession` row (`providerId='opencode'`).\n2. **Given** a session, **When** `client.sendPrompt(id, prompt)` runs, **Then** it dispatches the prompt and begins streaming `/event`.\n3. **Given** an SSE frame `{type:'text',part:{type:'text',text:'...'}}`, **When** parsed, **Then** a `ContentBlock` of type `text` is produced (reuses `parseOpencodeJson`).\n4. **Given** an SSE frame with `part.tool==='invalid'`, **When** parsed, **Then** a `PERMISSION_DENIED` block is produced.\n\n### User Story 3 - Ingest sessions into the local DB (Priority: P1)\n\nThe ingest engine consumes client events and projects them into the four OpenCode landing tables (`AgentSession`, `AgentPermissionDecision`, `AgentFileEdit`) **and** the durable `EventRecord` outbox (`source:'opencode'`). It also renders the session as a vivim chat thread via the Option C chat methods (`startAgentConversation`/`appendAgentMessage`/`getAgentMessages`), reusing `ConversationMessage`/`StreamBlock`. Governor permission decisions are applied programmatically: on a `/event` permission request, the ingest asks the Governor and replies via `POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID` (allow/deny), auto-denying any tool with risk tier > 3.\n\n**Why this priority**: This is the local-first payload — every served OpenCode session becomes durable, queryable, replayable vivim data without a second message table.\n\n**Independent Test**: `tests/integration/opencode/ingest.test.ts` (S1/S2) feeds recorded `serve` events and asserts: `AgentSession` + `AgentPermissionDecision` + `AgentFileEdit` rows written; `EventRecord` hash chain extended; a parallel `conversation` thread renders via `getAgentMessages`.\n\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\n\n1. **Given** a session-start event, **When** ingested, **Then** an `AgentSession` row exists (`providerId='opencode'`, `providerSessionId` from serve).\n2. **Given** a permission/tool request event, **When** ingested, **Then** an `AgentPermissionDecision` row exists (`providerPermissionId` unique, `riskTier` mapped) and the Governor decision is POSTed back.\n3. **Given** a file-diff event, **When** ingested, **Then** an `AgentFileEdit` row exists (`patchJson` RFC-6902, before/after hash).\n4. **Given** a text/step event, **When** ingested, **Then** `appendAgentMessage` appends to the session's `conversation` and `EventRecord` records the raw event (hash-chained).\n5. **Given** a duplicate event (same `providerPermissionId`/`providerMessageId`), **When** re-ingested, **Then** it is idempotent (no duplicate rows).\n\n### User Story 4 - Governor-owned permissions (Priority: P2)\n\nPermissions are resolved by the Governor in-process, NOT via `--auto` or frontmatter presets. Every permission event from `/event` triggers a Governor risk assessment; tier > 3 is auto-denied, others are delegated to the configured permission policy. The decision is recorded in `AgentPermissionDecision.decidedBy='governor'` and sent to OpenCode via `POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID`.\n\n**Why this priority**: Keeps the Governor as the single authority over tool execution (consistent with the rest of vivim), preventing OpenCode from silently approving risky tools.\n\n**Independent Test**: `tests/integration/opencode/permission.test.ts` (S2b) simulates a tier-4 bash permission event and asserts the decision is `deny` and the POST to the permissions endpoint carries `decision:'deny'`.\n\n**Acceptance Scenarios**:\n\n1. **Given** a permission request for `bash` rated tier 4, **When** the Governor assesses it, **Then** the decision is `deny` and `AgentPermissionDecision` reflects `decision:'deny'`, `decidedBy:'governor'`.\n2. **Given** a permission request for `read` rated tier 1, **When** assessed, **Then** the decision defaults to `allow` (or policy-resolved) and is POSTed back `decision:'allow'`.\n\n## Requirements\n\n- FR-1: Supervisor spawns `opencode serve` bound to `127.0.0.1` only, with password auth, default OFF.\n- FR-2: Supervisor handles the readiness race (poll until `GET /doc` 200) before declaring ready.\n- FR-3: Supervisor restarts on crash with bounded exponential backoff; This document\n> records the **projection contract** the ingest engine uses — it introduces NO new tables.\n\n## Reused Entities (no migration)\n\n### `AgentSession` (`prisma/schema.prisma:2967`)\n- `id` (ULID), `providerSessionId` (unique), `providerId` (default `'opencode'`), `parentSessionId` (fork tree), `agentName`, `model`, `projectPath`, `status`.\n- **Ingest writes**: one row per served OpenCode session. `providerSessionId` = serve `sessionId`; `providerId='opencode'`; `status` ∈ `active|idle|closed`.\n\n### `AgentPermissionDecision` (`prisma/schema.prisma:~2985`)\n- `id`, `agentSessionId` (FK cascade), `providerPermissionId` (unique), `toolName`, `riskTier` (1-5 → `Node.securityLevel`), `requestedAt`, `respondedAt?`, `decision` (`allow|deny|allow_always`), `decidedBy?`, `payloadJson`.\n- **Ingest writes**: one row per `/event` permission request. `riskTier` mapped from tool/permission; `decidedBy='governor'`; `decision` from Governor assessment.\n\n### `AgentFileEdit` (`prisma/schema.prisma:~2998`)\n- `id`, `agentSessionId` (FK cascade), `messageId?`, `filePath`, `patchJson` (RFC-6902 JSON Patch), `beforeHash?`, `afterHash?`.\n- **Ingest writes**: one row per file-diff event from `GET /session/:id/diff`. `patchJson` = RFC-6902 ops.\n\n### `EventRecord` (`src/engines/event-record-store.ts`)\n- `id`, `seq` (monotonic per source), `source` (`'opencode'`), `type`, `entityType?`, `entityId?`, `providerSessionId?`, `payloadJson`, `prevHash`, `hash`.\n- **Ingest writes**: every raw served event → one `EventRecord` (`source:'opencode'`, hash-chained). Single source of truth for replay.\n\n### `Conversation` / `ConversationMessage` / `StreamBlock` (Option C)\n- Reused via `AgenticStoreContract.startAgentConversation` / `appendAgentMessage` / `getAgentMessages`.\n- `startAgentConversation` → `{providerSessionId, conversationId}`; creates `Conversation` with `providerId='opencode'` and an opening user message.\n- `appendAgentMessage(conversationId, {role,text,blocks?,model?,authorDid?,stepId?})` → `{id}`.\n\n### `ProviderSession` / `ProviderDefinition`\n- `providerId='opencode'` already seeded by feature `022` (`capability-bootstrap.ts`). Ingest creates a `ProviderSession` (or reuses the seeded one) and links `AgentSession.providerSessionId` → it.\n\n## Ingest Projection Contract\n\n```text\nserve SSE event\n  ├─ session_start      → AgentSession (status='active')            + EventRecord\n  ├─ text / step         → appendAgentMessage(role,text,blocks)      + EventRecord\n  ├─ tool_use (invalid)  → AgentPermissionDecision(deny, PERMISSION) + EventRecord\n  ├─ permission_request  → AgentPermissionDecision(<tier>)           + Governor assess\n  │                        → POST /session/:id/permissions/:pid      (allow|deny)\n  ├─ diff                → AgentFileEdit(patchJson, hashes)         + EventRecord\n  └─ session_end         → AgentSession(status='closed')            + EventRecord\n```\n\n## State Transitions\n\n- `AgentSession.status`: `idle → active → closed`.\n- `AgentPermissionDecision.decision`: `pending (on request) → allow | deny | allow_always (after Governor)`.\n\n## Idempotency Keys\n\n- `AgentSession`: `providerSessionId` (unique constraint).\n- `AgentPermissionDecision`: `providerPermissionId` (unique constraint).\n- `AgentFileEdit`: `(agentSessionId, filePath, messageId?)`.\n- `EventRecord`: hash chain `prevHash || payloadJson` — duplicate payloads produce identical hash; ingest dedupes by `providerMessageId`/`providerPermissionId` before append.\n\n## Risk Tier Mapping (Governor)\n\n| Tool family        | riskTier | Auto-deny (tier>3) |\n|--------------------|----------|--------------------|\n| read / view        | 1        | no                 |\n| edit (allowed path)| 2        | no                 |\n| web fetch          | 3        | no                 |\n| bash / exec        | 4        | **yes**            |\n| filesystem delete  | 5        | **yes**            |\n",

{
  "content": "# Contracts: OpenCode `serve` Client API\n\n**Feature**: `027-opencode-serve` | **Date**: 2026-07-19\n\n> The authoritative contract is the live OpenAPI at `GET /doc` of a running `opencode serve`.\n> This document pins the subset the vivim client depends on (verified against opencode v1.17.15).\n\n## Base URL & Auth\n\n- Base: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (loopback only).\n- Auth: HTTP Basic. User `OPENCODE_SERVER_USERNAME` (default `opencode`), password `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`.\n- All requests include `Authorization: Basic base64(user:password)`.\n\n## Endpoints\n\n### `GET /doc`\n- Returns OpenAPI 3.1 JSON. Used as the **readiness probe** (200 = server up) and schema source.\n- Client: `await fetch(base + '/doc', {headers: auth})`.\n\n### `GET /global/health`\n- Liveness. Supervisor polls this (or `/doc`) until 200 before declaring ready.\n\n### `POST /session`\n- Body: `{ message?: string, cwd?: string, agent?: string, model?: string }`.\n- Response: `{ id: string, ... }` — the `sessionId` (→ `AgentSession.providerSessionId`).\n\n### `POST /session/:id/message`\n- Body: `{ message: string }`.\n- Sends a turn synchronously. Response 200 = accepted.\n\n### `POST /session/:id/prompt_async`\n- Body: `{ prompt: string }`.\n- Async dispatch; streamed via `GET /event`. Response 202 = queued.\n\n### `GET /event` (SSE)\n- `Accept: text/event-stream`. Streams session events.\n- Each frame is a JSON object with top-level `type` and `part` (same grammar as `--format json`).\n- Client parses each frame via `parseOpencodeJson`.\n\n### `GET /session/:id/diff`\n- Returns file diffs for the session. Source of `AgentFileEdit.patchJson` (RFC-6902).\n\n### `POST /session/:id/permissions/:permissionID`\n- Body: `{ decision: 'allow' | 'deny' | 'allow_always' }`.\n- Governor replies here for each `/event` permission request.\n\n## SSE Frame → ContentBlock Mapping (reuse `parseOpencodeJson`)\n\n| frame `type` / `part.type` | ContentBlock |\n|----------------------------|--------------|\n| `text` / `part.type:'text'` | `{type:'text',text}` |\n| `reasoning` | `{type:'reasoning',text}` |\n| `step-start` | `{type:'step-start'}` |\n| `tool` (valid) | `{type:'tool-call',...}` + `{type:'tool-result',...}` |\n| `tool` (`part.tool==='invalid'`) | `{type:'error',code:'PERMISSION_DENIED',message}` |\n| `error` | `{type:'error',code:'AGENT_FAILED',message}` |\n\n## Client Interface (TypeScript)\n\n```ts\nexport interface OpenCodeClient {\n  ready(): Promise<void>                                  // poll /doc until 200\n  createSession(opts: { cwd?: string; model?: string; message?: string }): Promise<{ sessionId: string }>\n  sendPrompt(sessionId: string, prompt: string): Promise<void>\n  subscribe(sessionId: string, onEvent: (ev: OpencodeEvent) => void): Promise<() => void>\n  respondPermission(sessionId: string, permissionId: string, decision: 'allow' | 'deny' | 'allow_always'): Promise<void>\n  getDiff(sessionId: string): Promise<unknown>\n}\n```\n\n## Supervisor Interface (TypeScript)\n\n```ts\nexport interface OpenCodeSupervisor {\n  start(): Promise<{ port: number }>\n  stop(): Promise<void>\n  isRunning(): boolean\n  on(event: 'ready' | 'exit' | 'error', cb: (info: unknown) => void): void\n}\n```\n",

- `AgentSession` has NO `conversationId` field — conversation linked only via `ProviderSession` (`providerSessionId` on both `Conversation` and `AgentSession`); ingest looks up conversation by `providerSessionId`.
- Reuse `parseOpencodeJson` from `src/engines/local-agent/local-agent-executor.ts` for SSE→`ContentBlock[]` (verified same grammar as `--format json`).
- Risk tiers: read=1, edit=2, web/fetch=3, bash/exec=4 (auto-deny), delete/rm=5 (auto-deny).
- `EventRecordStore` is the single source of truth (hash-chained, `source:'opencode'`); OpenCode landing tables are projections.

The supervisor invokes it as\n// `launcher serve --port <p> --hostname 127.0.0.1`, so we drop the literal\n// 'serve' token (the shim doesn't need it) and forward port/hostname.\nconst LAUNCHER = `\nimport { spawn } from 'node:child_process'\nconst i = process.argv.indexOf('--port')\nconst port = process.argv[i + 1]\nconst h = process.argv[process.argv.indexOf('--hostname') + 1]\nconst child = spawn('bun', [process.env.SHIM_PATH, 'serve', '--port', port, '--hostname', h], { stdio: 'inherit' })\nchild.unref()\nawait new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 200))\nprocess.exit(0)\n`\n\nbeforeAll(() => {\n  dir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'opencode-superv-'))\n  shimPath = join(dir, 'serve-shim.ts')\n  launcherPath = join(dir, 'launcher.ts')\n  writeFileSync(shimPath, SHIM)\n  writeFileSync(launcherPath, LAUNCHER)\n  process.env.SHIM_PATH = shimPath\n})\n\nafterAll(() => {\n  rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true })\n})\n\ndescribe('S3: supervisor lifecycle', () => {\n  it('starts serve (loopback + password), probes readiness, stops cleanly', async () => {\n    const supervisor = new OpenCodeSupervisor({\n      enabled: true,\n      binary: 'bun',\n      cwd: dir,\n      password: 'test',\n      username: 'opencode',\n      // Inject launcher via environment so the supervisor's argv becomes\n      // `bun launcher.ts serve --port <p> --hostname 127.0.0.1`.\n      extraArgs: [launcherPath, 'serve'],\n    })\n    expect(typeof supervisor.start).toBe('function')\n    let port = 0\n    try {\n      const ready = await supervisor.start()\n      port = ready.port\n      expect(port).toBeGreaterThan(0)\n      expect(supervisor.isRunning()).toBe(true)\n      const res = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/doc`, {\n        headers: { Authorization: `Basic ${Buffer.from('opencode:test').toString('base64')}` },\n      })\n      expect(res.ok).toBe(true)\n    } finally {\n      await supervisor.stop()\n    }\n    expect(supervisor.isRunning()).toBe(false)\n  })\n})\n",
